description: Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, security risks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks in Claude Code, Codex, and MCP skills before you install them.
readme_content:
# SkillSpector

**Security scanner for AI agent skills.** Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, and security risks before installing agent skills.

[![Python 3.12+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)

## Overview

AI agent skills (used by Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, etc.) execute with implicit trust and minimal vetting. In the 31,132-skill analyzed subset of the research dataset, **26.1% of skills contain vulnerabilities** and **5.2% show likely malicious intent**.

SkillSpector helps you answer: **"Is this skill safe to install?"**

SkillSpector is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/), which scans, evaluates, and signs agent skills before publication. Skills that pass are published to the [NVIDIA skills catalog](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills).

## Documentation

- **[Scan agent skills before installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/scanning-agent-skills)** — Hosted guide: when to scan, how to read a report, and how to gate installs.
- **[Development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)** — Architecture, package layout, and how to extend the analyzer pipeline.
- **[Security policy](SECURITY.md)** — Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to NVIDIA PSIRT.
- **[Analysis resource bounds](docs/ANALYSIS_RESOURCE_BOUNDS.md)** — Fail-closed bundle, parser, nested-artifact, ledger, and finding ceilings.
- **[Pi extension](docs/PI_EXTENSION.md)** — Install SkillSpector as a Pi tool for scanning skills from inside agent sessions.
- **[OpenCode extension](docs/OPENCODE_EXTENSION.md)** — Install SkillSpector as an OpenCode tool and `/skillspector` command for scanning skills from inside agent sessions.

## Features

- **Multi-format input**: Scan Git repos, URLs, zip files, directories, or single files
- **71 vulnerability patterns** across 17 categories: prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply chain, excessive agency, output handling, system prompt leakage, memory poisoning, tool misuse, rogue agent, anti-refusal, trigger abuse, dangerous code (AST), taint tracking, YARA signatures, MCP least privilege, and MCP tool poisoning
- **Two-stage analysis**: Fast static analysis + optional LLM semantic evaluation
- **Live vulnerability lookups**: SC4 queries [OSV.dev](https://osv.dev) for real-time CVE data with automatic offline fallback
- **Multiple output formats**: Terminal, JSON, Markdown, and SARIF reports
- **Risk scoring**: 0-100 score with severity labels and clear recommendations
- **Baseline / false-positive suppression**: Accept known findings via a glob-rule or fingerprint baseline so re-scans surface only *new* issues ([docs](docs/SUPPRESSION.md))

## Quick Start

### Installation

> **Open-source software notice:** This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use.

Create and activate a virtual environment first (all `make` targets assume the venv is active). Use **uv** or **pip**; the Makefile uses `uv` if available, otherwise `pip`.

**Quick install with uv (CLI-only):**

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git
# Update later: uv tool update skillspector
```

If you plan to run `skillspector mcp`, install the MCP extra at install time:

```bash
uv tool install 'skillspector[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git'
```

**From source:**

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git
cd skillspector

# Create and activate virtual environment
uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
# or: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate

# Install for production use
make install
```

To contribute, follow the [Development setup](#setup) for a supported Python
interpreter and development dependencies.

### Docker (no Python required)

Run SkillSpector without installing Python by building it locally from the included [Dockerfile](Dockerfile). The image is based on the Docker Official Python `3.12-slim-bookworm` image.

**Build the image:**

```bash
make docker-build
# or: docker build -t skillspector .
```

**Scan a local directory** by mounting your current directory into `/scan`, the container's working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/scan" skillspector scan ./my-skill/ --no-llm
```

**Scan with LLM analysis** by passing credentials with a local `.env` file:

```bash
cat > .env <<'EOF'
SKILLSPECTOR_PROVIDER=anthropic
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
EOF
```

```bash
docker run --rm \
  -v "$PWD:/scan" \
  --env-file .env \
  skillspector scan ./my-skill/
```

Or pass credentials directly from your shell environment:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  -v "$PWD:/scan" \
  -e SKILLSPECTOR_PROVIDER=anthropic \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  skillspector scan ./my-skill/
```

**Write a report to the host filesystem** by writing to the mounted directory:

```bash
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -v "$PWD:/scan" \
  skillspector scan ./my-skill/ --no-llm --format json --output report.json
```

**Optional alias** for repeated static scans:

```bash
alias skillspector-docker='docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/scan" skillspector'
skillspector-docker scan ./my-skill/ --no-llm
```

### Basic Usage

```bash
# Scan a local skill directory
skillspector scan ./my-skill/

# Scan a single SKILL.md file
skillspector scan ./SKILL.md

# Scan a Git repository
skillspector scan https://github.com/user/my-skill

# Scan a zip file
skillspector scan ./my-skill.zip
```

#### Size limits

SkillSpector enforces two independent caps on remote and archive inputs to bound the impact of oversized downloads and zip bombs:

- **Per-ingest cap**: `INGEST_MAX_BYTES` (100 MiB) — applied to streamed URL downloads, total uncompressed size of zip archives, and post-clone disk usage of Git repos.
- **Zip member cap**: `INGEST_MAX_ZIP_MEMBERS` (10,000) — caps the number of entries in a single zip.

Note that the per-file 1 MB analysis cap (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`) is a separate, downstream limit: it bounds what individual analyzers will read out of an already-ingested directory. The ingest caps above bound how much content can land on disk in the first place. A breach of either ingest cap fails closed with an `IngestLimitExceededError`.

### Output Formats

```bash
# Terminal output (default) - pretty formatted
skillspector scan ./my-skill/

# JSON output - machine readable
skillspector scan ./my-skill/ --format json --output report.json

# Markdown output - for documentation
skillspector scan ./my-skill/ --format markdown --output report.md

# SARIF output - for CI/CD integration and IDE tooling
skillspector scan ./my-skill/ --format sarif --output report.sarif
```

### Recursive Collection Scanning

`--recursive` scans immediate subdirectories containing `SKILL.md` as independent
skills, with a default aggregate limit of **32 skills**. To raise or lower it:

```bash
skillspector scan ./my-skills/ --recursive --max-skills 100 --no-llm --format json
```

`--max-skills` requires a local recursive collection and a positive integer; `0`
does not mean unlimited. Discovery, byte, finding-record, time and report-size
budgets still apply, so increasing the count does not guarantee complete coverage.
When the count limit is reached, the CLI names the limit and suggests adjusting it
or scanning sub-skills separately. Omitted skills remain visible in the aggregate
report and coverage stays incomplete. Use `--fail-on-incomplete` in CI to fail on
incomplete coverage; the default exit policy is unchanged.

### Batch Scanning

Scan entire directories of skills in parallel from `contrib/batch_scan/`:

```bash
python -m contrib.batch_scan.batch_scan ./my-skills/ --no-llm
python -m contrib.batch_scan.batch_scan ./my-skills/ --workers 20 -f json -o report.json
python -m contrib.batch_scan.batch_scan ./tests/fixtures/ -f terminal --workers 20
```

Supports multilingual detection (zh/ja/ko) and terminal/JSON/Markdown output.

For LLM scans with higher concurrency, configure multiple API keys following
[`.env.example`](contrib/batch_scan/.env.example) — the pool improves throughput
and resilience, provided the keys don't share an account-level rate limit.

See the [contrib guide](contrib/batch_scan/docs/) for details.

> **Note on LLM support:** The default configuration targets DeepSeek as the
> cheapest public option. DeepSeek-Chat is
> [expected to sunset](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/), and the contributor
> does not have hardware to test against local models. The batch scanner was
> originally tested with OpenAI-compatible endpoints — DeepSeek's lack of
> structured-output support required manual JSON-parsing patches. If you can
> contribute a more universal backend (Ollama, vLLM, or a different provider),
> PRs are very welcome.

### Comparing MCP Registry snapshots

A named scan fetches only that server's published versions from the official
registry, then selects entries marked as latest. If none are marked as latest,
all matching versions are assessed. The server name remains the report source:

```bash
skillspector scan 'ac.inference.sh/mcp' --mcp-registry --format json --output current.json
```

Use `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers` as the input to scan
the full catalog. Local registry captures are also supported.

Start with raw registry payload captures (`registry-before.json` and
`registry-after.json`). Save a scan report as `previous.json`, then compare a
later scan against that generated local report:

```bash
skillspector scan registry-before.json --mcp-registry --format json --output previous.json
skillspector scan registry-after.json --mcp-registry --format json \
  --mcp-registry-compare previous.json --output compared.json
```

The optional `comparison` object lists added and removed server identities,
changed normalized fields with their previous and current values, and an
`unchanged_count`. Identity is the server name and version, so a new version
appears as an addition and the old version as a removal if it is absent from the
new scan. Acquisition source and scan timestamp are excluded from comparison.
`unmodeled_changes` lists same-identity records whose raw-record hash changed
while normalized fields match; these are not counted as unchanged. This can
indicate a change to fields outside the snapshot model, or array reordering in
the raw record. Package and remote ordering alone is not a normalized field change.
Entries in `changed` may also contain changes outside the snapshot model; inspect
the raw record to see those changes.
Compare reports with the same selection scope: a server absent from the current
input is reported as removed, which does not prove it was removed from a registry.

The comparison file must be a local report produced by this registry mode with
valid normalized snapshots. Malformed, oversized or duplicate server identities
are rejected. This option requires `--mcp-registry` and is separate from the
finding-suppression `--baseline`: it never suppresses findings or changes risk
scores, and it does not fetch or execute listed server endpoints.

Registry mode rejects skill-only controls such as `--use-shipped-baseline`,
`--transitive`, `--transitive-depth`, `--transitive-allow-prefix`, and
`--transitive-deny-prefix` with exit code 2, including an explicitly supplied
default depth (`--transitive-depth 1`). Omit these options for registry scans.

### Suppressing False Positives (baseline)

Suppress known/accepted findings so the risk score reflects only un-triaged
issues and re-scans surface only *new* findings. See the
[suppression guide](docs/SUPPRESSION.md) for the full reference.

```bash
# Accept all current findings into a baseline (run once), then commit it.
skillspector baseline ./my-skill/ -

readme_content:
# HermesEnabler 2

[English](README.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Português](README.pt.md)

![](image.png)

> Supported only on watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1.

## Installation

### Install the IPA

1. Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/pookjw/HermesEnabler/releases).
2. Install it with [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io).
3. On your iPhone, open the **Watch** app and install **HermesEnabler2** from **My Watch → Apps**.
4. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app.

### Build with Xcode

1. Open [HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj](HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj) in Xcode.
2. Select your Apple Watch as the run destination and click **Run**.
3. Open **HermesEnabler2** on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app.

## Cautions

- In Sideloadly, disable **Use automatic bundle ID** and use a fixed Bundle Identifier. Keep the same Bundle Identifier and Apple ID for every update so the app can retain its existing data and backup.
- Before deleting the app, always restore your MobileGestalt backup through the HermesEnabler2 app.

## Credits

This project incorporates code from [Gester](https://github.com/sasobhabha/Gester).

Use at your own risk.

# OpenBot ### AI coworkers. Ready for the enterprise. A modular, self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers.
Choose your models. Bring your agents. Own your infrastructure. [open.bot](https://open.bot) · [Docs](docs/README.md) · [Deploy on Kubernetes](#deploy-on-kubernetes) · [Run from source](#run-from-source) [![GitHub Trending: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/175080)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080) [![Trendshift: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/trendshift/repositories/175080/daily)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080)
[![Download for Mac (Apple silicon)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Mac%20%28Apple%20silicon%29&color=6E6AE0)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) [![Download for Mac (Intel)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Mac%20%28Intel%29&color=4A7CC8)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) [![Download for Windows](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Windows&color=9A5CC6)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) Notarized .dmg for Apple silicon and Intel Macs · signed installer for Windows x64 · no terminal or developer tools needed · [Release notes](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/latest)
[![OpenBot for Business: get early access](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenBot_for_Business-Get_early_access_%E2%86%92-D14B9C?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466)](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) From [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), creators of [AG-UI](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui).
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c60f07da-8b6d-46eb-a573-17fc1e65a644

Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm chart deploys both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](charts/openbot/README.md) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. The chart installs Intelligence by default; no separate hosted project is required. For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with **amd64 nodes**, a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, cluster sizing, or an existing Intelligence deployment, use the [full Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and [the Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). readme_content:
# llama.cpp ![llama.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama-brand/refs/heads/master/logo/svg/cover/llama-cpp/cover-llama-cpp-dark.svg)
LLM inference in C/C++ [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ggml-org/llama.cpp?filter=v*&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases?q=tag:v0) [![Nightly](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ggml-org/llama.cpp?label=nightly&filter=b*&color=orange)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases?q=b) [![Server](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/ggml-org/llama.cpp/server.yml?label=Server)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/actions/workflows/server.yml) [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/ggml-org/llama.cpp/docker.yml?label=Docker)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/actions/workflows/docker.yml) [![Winget](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/ggml-org/llama.cpp/winget.yml?label=Winget)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/actions/workflows/winget.yml) [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml) / [ops](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/ops.md) / [maintainer PRs](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20draft%3AFalse%20(author%3Asanmai%20OR%20author%3Argerganov%20OR%20author%3AKitaitiMakoto%20OR%20author%3Adanbev%20OR%20author%3Aaldehir%20OR%20author%3Amax-krasnyansky%20OR%20author%3ACISC%20OR%20author%3Aggerganov%20OR%20author%3Aam17an%20OR%20author%3Ajhen0409%20OR%20author%3Abartowski1182%20OR%20author%3Anikwen%20OR%20author%3Ahipudding%20OR%20author%3Aravi9%20OR%20author%3AServeurpersoCom%20OR%20author%3Athelittlefireman%20OR%20author%3Apwilkin%20OR%20author%3Areeselevine%20OR%20author%3Angxson%20OR%20author%3Ajeffbolznv%20OR%20author%3Amarty1885%20OR%20author%3A0cc4m%20OR%20author%3ATitaniumtown%20OR%20author%3Aangt%20OR%20author%3AIMbackK%20OR%20author%3Aarthw%20OR%20author%3AJohannesGaessler%20OR%20author%3AORippler%20OR%20author%3Aruixiang63%20OR%20author%3Axctan%20OR%20author%3AmasterFoad%20OR%20author%3Aallozaur%20OR%20author%3AAndreas-Krebbel%20OR%20author%3Ayomaytk%20OR%20author%3Aaendk%20OR%20author%3Awine99%20OR%20author%3Agaugarg-nv%20OR%20author%3Ataronaeo%20OR%20author%3Aforforever73%20OR%20author%3Achaxu01%20OR%20author%3Alhez%20OR%20author%3AAlekseiNikiforovIBM%20OR%20author%3Anetrunnereve%20OR%20author%3Afairydreaming%20OR%20author%3Aynankani)%20sort%3Aupdated-desc) / [dev stats](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp-dev) / [lib llama API](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/9289) / [llama-server REST API](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/9291)
## Quick start A few options to get `llama.cpp` installed on your machine: ```bash # curl curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh # powershell irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex ``` - Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions - Run with Docker - see our [Docker documentation](docs/docker.md) - Download pre-built binaries from the [releases page](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases) - Build from source by cloning this repository - check out [our build guide](docs/build.md) Once installed: ```sh # Download and run a model directly from Hugging Face llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF # Launch OpenAI-compatible API server llama serve -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF ```
VLM session with llama cli Built-in web UI against llama serve
## Description The main goal of `llama.cpp` is to enable LLM (and VLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware - locally and in the cloud. - Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies - Apple silicon is a first-class citizen - optimized via ARM NEON, Accelerate and Metal frameworks - AVX, AVX2, AVX512 and AMX support for x86 architectures - RVV, ZVFH, ZFH, ZICBOP and ZIHINTPAUSE support for RISC-V architectures - 1.5-bit, 2-bit, 3-bit, 4-bit, 5-bit, 6-bit, and 8-bit integer quantization for faster inference and reduced memory use - Custom CUDA kernels for running LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs (support for AMD GPUs via HIP and Moore Threads GPUs via MUSA) - Vulkan and SYCL backend support - CPU+GPU hybrid inference to partially accelerate models larger than the total VRAM capacity The `llama.cpp` project is build on top of the [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml) library. ## Supported backends | Backend | Target devices | | --- | --- | | [BLAS](docs/build.md#blas-build) | All | | [BLIS](docs/backend/BLIS.md) | All | | [CANN](docs/build.md#cann) | Huawei Ascend NPU | | [CUDA](docs/build.md#cuda) | Nvidia GPU | | [HIP](docs/build.md#hip) | AMD GPU | | [Hexagon](docs/backend/snapdragon/README.md) | Snapdragon | | [IBM zDNN](docs/backend/zDNN.md) | IBM Z & LinuxONE | | [MUSA](docs/build.md#musa) | Moore Threads GPU | | [Metal](docs/build.md#metal-build) | Apple Silicon | | [OpenCL](docs/backend/OPENCL.md) | Adreno GPU | | [OpenVINO [In Progress]](docs/backend/OPENVINO.md) | Intel CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs | | [RPC](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/rpc) | All | | [SYCL](docs/backend/SYCL.md) | Intel GPU | | [VirtGPU](docs/backend/VirtGPU.md) | VirtGPU APIR | | [Vulkan](docs/build.md#vulkan) | GPU | | [WebGPU](docs/build.md#webgpu) | All | | [ZenDNN](docs/build.md#zendnn) | AMD CPU | ## Documentation #### Tools - [cli](tools/cli/README.md) - [completion](tools/completion/README.md) - [server](tools/server/README.md) - [GBNF grammars](grammars/README.md) #### Development - [How to build](docs/build.md) - [Running on Docker](docs/docker.md) - [Build on Android](docs/android.md) - [Multi-GPU usage](docs/multi-gpu.md) - [Performance troubleshooting](docs/development/token_generation_performance_tips.md) - [GGML tips & tricks](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/wiki/GGML-Tips-&-Tricks) - [XCFramework](docs/xcframework.md) - [Completions](docs/completions.md) - [Models](docs/models.md) - [Release process](docs/release.md) ## Contributing - Contributors can open PRs - Collaborators will be invited based on contributions - Maintainers can push to branches in the `llama.cpp` repo and merge PRs into the `master` branch - Any help with managing issues, PRs and projects is very appreciated! - Read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information ## Acknowledgements - readme_content:
![Banner image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8n-io/n8n/master/assets/readme-banner.jpg)

# n8n – The Platform for AI Agents and Workflow Automation

Fair-code platform to build and deploy AI agents and workflows. Combine a visual canvas with custom code, run it self-hosted or in the [cloud](https://app.n8n.cloud/login), and connect to 1500+ integrations. AI automation you can trust with real work, from prototype to production.

![n8n.io - Screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8n-io/n8n/master/assets/n8n-screenshot-readme.png)

## Key Capabilities

- **AI-Native Automation Platform**: Build and operationalize AI workflows and multi-step agents using your own data, models, and tools
- **Model Flexibility, No Lock-In**: Connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or open-source models and switch providers without changing your architecture
- **From Prototype to Production**: Design multi-step AI workflows with logic, tool use, human approvals, and full observability
- **Code When You Need It**: Combine visual building with JavaScript, Python, and npm packages for advanced AI workflows
- **Enterprise-Ready AI**: Self-host or deploy securely with role-based access, audit trails, and support for sensitive data
- **Leverage What Already Exists**: 1500+ integrations and 9,000+ workflow [templates](https://n8n.io/workflows) to connect AI with your existing systems

## Quick Start

Try n8n instantly with our install script (requires [Docker](https://www.docker.com/)):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.n8n.io | sh
```

Or deploy manually with [Docker](https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/installation/docker/):

```
docker volume create n8n_data
docker run -it --rm --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n
```

Access the editor at http://localhost:5678

## Resources

- 📚 [Documentation](https://docs.n8n.io)
- 🔧 [1500+ Integrations](https://n8n.io/integrations)
- 💡 [Example Workflows](https://n8n.io/workflows)
- 🤖 [AI & LangChain Guide](https://docs.n8n.io/advanced-ai/)
- 👥 [Community Forum](https://community.n8n.io)
- 📖 [Community Tutorials](https://community.n8n.io/c/tutorials/28)

## Support

Need help? Our community forum is the place to get support and connect with other users:
[community.n8n.io](https://community.n8n.io)

## License

n8n is [fair-code](https://faircode.io) distributed under the [Sustainable Use License](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/LICENSE.md) and [n8n Enterprise License](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/LICENSE_EE.md).

- **Source Available**: Always visible source code
- **Self-Hostable**: Deploy anywhere
- **Extensible**: Add your own nodes and functionality

[Enterprise Licenses](mailto:license@n8n.io) available for additional features and support.

Additional information about the license model can be found in the [docs](https://docs.n8n.io/n8n-community-license/).

## Contributing

Found a bug 🐛 or have a feature idea ✨? Check our [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for a setup guide & best practices.

## Join the Team

Want to shape the future of automation? Check out our [job posts](https://n8n.io/careers) and join our team!

## What does n8n mean?

**Short answer:** It means "nodemation" and is pronounced as n-eight-n.

**Long answer:** "I get that question quite often (more often than I expected) so I decided it is probably best to answer it here. While looking for a good name for the project with a free domain I realized very quickly that all the good ones I could think of were already taken. So, in the end, I chose nodemation. 'node-' in the sense that it uses a Node-View and that it uses Node.js and '-mation' for 'automation' which is what the project is supposed to help with. However, I did not like how long the name was and I could not imagine writing something that long every time in the CLI. That is when I then ended up on 'n8n'." - **Jan Oberhauser, Founder and CEO, n8n.io**

readme_content:
# Locally Uncensored **The all-in-one local AI studio for your desktop. Chat, images, video and a coding agent in one app. Install it, pick a model, go.** Free and open source. In local mode everything runs on your own machine. No Docker, no terminal, no config files. The platforms are listed under [Download](#download). [![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL%20v3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored?style=social)](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/stargazers) [![GitHub last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored)](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/commits) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored) [![CodeQL](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/actions/workflows/codeql.yml) [![GitHub Discussions](https://img.shields.io/github/discussions/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored)](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/discussions) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1496087522042843146?style=flat-square&logo=discord&label=Discord&color=5865F2)](https://locallyuncensored.com/discord) [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-locallyuncensored.com-8b5cf6)](https://locallyuncensored.com) [Download](#download) · [Three steps](#three-steps) · [What is in the box](#what-is-in-the-box) · [How it compares](#how-it-compares) · [Models](#models-that-run-well) · [FAQ](#faq) | Chat that draws your images | Images and video in the same window | |:---:|:---:| | ![Chat](docs/screenshots/chat_generate_dark.webp) | ![Create](docs/screenshots/create_gallery_dark.webp) | | **The coding agent shows the diff first** | **Agent mode does the legwork** | | ![Coding agent](docs/screenshots/coding_review_dark.webp) | ![Agent mode](docs/screenshots/agent_mode_dark.webp) |
--- ## Download Take the latest build from [Releases](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/latest). | Platform | File | Status | |----------|------|--------| | Windows 10 and 11 | [`Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_x64-setup.exe`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/latest/download/Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_x64-setup.exe) (NSIS, recommended) or [`Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_x64_en-US.msi`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/latest/download/Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_x64_en-US.msi) | Tested every release, signed auto update channel | | Linux | [`Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_amd64.AppImage`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/latest/download/Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_amd64.AppImage), [`Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_amd64.deb`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/latest/download/Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_amd64.deb) or [`Locally.Uncensored-3.0.10-1.x86_64.rpm`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/latest/download/Locally.Uncensored-3.0.10-1.x86_64.rpm) | Built on every release | | macOS 14 or newer, Apple Silicon (Beta) | [`LU_3.0.10_aarch64.dmg`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/download/v3.0.10/LU_3.0.10_aarch64.dmg) | Signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Intel Macs are not supported. The app has run on one Mac so far. Voice has been tried by hand in the app on a Mac and works. Computer control is in the Mac app but not fully tested yet on macOS. Remote Access and the automatic update are not confirmed on macOS | | Android 7.0 or newer (arm64) | [`LU-3.0.10-Android.apk`](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/download/v3.0.10/LU-3.0.10-Android.apk) | The phone app. Not in the Play Store yet: install the file from this page. SHA-256 `dbd515d81bbc8ab70f21b850424f9f8b57ae88ae24962225beefc4116d139d2f` | Some antivirus engines flag unsigned NSIS installers that download other binaries, which is a false positive. The installer is built by GitHub Actions from the public source on `master`, and the update channel is signed against a public minisign key, so you can verify both: see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#antivirus--browser-false-positives). Code signing for the Windows installers: free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org). SignPath Foundation has accepted the project. The production certificate is not in place yet, and until it is the installers ship unsigned. Current release: **v3.0.10** (November 2026). Every change since 1.0.0 is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). 3.0.10 fixes lost chats from 3.0.8 and 3.0.9. A backup no longer replaces the only complete copy of your chats, a note at launch says when the backup holds chats that are missing from your list, and Settings, Chat Backup has Restore chats from backup. The Android app is back as an APK, with the keyboard staying open in the Create prompt. 3.0.9 brings Liquid's LFM3 models for small machines: 1.7B and 2B, about 1 to 1.7 GB each, for text, pictures and speech, on the LU Engine, on Ollama or as MLX builds on a Mac; the LU Engine moves to llama.cpp b11960 for them. A group chat now sends every speaker the context you picked, can redo one speaker and lets you set who speaks when. A compaction is one quiet line in the chat, and the conversation before it stays one click away. Animate takes an end image and, with MiniMax H3, up to nine reference pictures, and Krea 2, Qwen-Image 2.1 and FLUX.2 take reference pictures for a style, a person or a pose. Local videos run up to 15 seconds without drifting in colour, and a video shows a rough preview while it renders. The trainer learns a style, a concept or a pose next to a character (Beta). "Use this model" on Hugging Face opens the download in LU, and a model from the search comes in a quant that fits your graphics card. A status menu sits in the Mac menu bar and the Windows and Linux tray, and the Linux AppImage starts again on systems without the tray library. What has only run in automated tests is listed under Known limits in the [release notes](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/tag/v3.0.9). 3.0.8 makes web search in the chat work again: LU asks five search services in turn and needs no key for any of them. A video made in the chat plays in the chat, and a long one renders in the background while you write on. A picture attached in the chat reaches the image tool, and with two graphics cards chat and ComfyUI can each get their own. The LU Engine plans a model's memory from the file itself and offers a shorter context with one click. AMD cards on Windows get AMD's current ROCm build. New: the chat can read and change LU's settings with a confirmation card, the Model Manager can make a copy of a local model that refuses less, and Settings, Storage puts models, gallery and runtime in one folder of your choice. What has only run in automated tests is listed under Known limits in the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md). 3.0.5 was about Create: LTX 2.5, FastH3 and YuE2 run on your own machine, Qwen-Image 2.1 gets a transparent background and its prompt enhancer, Edit, Remove Background and Enhance Image take up to 50 images in one go, and LU Cloud adds Qwen Image 2.1, LTX 2.5, MiniMax H3 and Wan 3.0 Reference. Chat takes any file, each model in a group chat can have its own persona, dropdowns stay inside the window (issue 149), and the speech install works again on Ubuntu 24.04. 3.0.4 fixed the Code agent and the agent in chat on LU Cloud: writing a long file no longer ends the run, "continue" picks up where a run stopped instead of starting over, the agent keeps a plan only when you ask for one, and cloud context is 32K by default and can be set per model. It also fixed the bugs reported on GitHub and Discord since 3.0.3 (issues 144 to 147): MiniMax H3 runs as a video model with sound, Edit takes up to three extra images with Qwen-Image 2.1, a missing encoder or VAE is named and offered as a download instead of ending in "Value not in list", the LoRA stack follows the loras folder, and group chat works with every LU Engine model. 3.0.3 was a hotfix: chats with many images no longer run the app out of memory, Create reads a model's family from the file instead of its name, and the five bugs reported on GitHub since 3.0.2 are fixed (issues 139 to 143). 3.0.2 was a hotfix: the Code tab lost its scrollbar and its input box once a conversation grew taller than the window (issue 138, a regression in 3.0.1) and is held to the window height again, and the count of open cloud models now takes the Create Studio endpoints in, which makes it fourteen video models and seven image models. ### What is new in 3.0.1 - **Qwen-Image 2.1 runs locally on Windows and Linux.** One model generates a picture from a prompt and edits one from a reference image, with no mask to paint. About 16 GB of files, ComfyUI 0.37.0 or newer, and a research license that does not allow commercial use. - **Models has a LoRAs tab of its own.** Search CivitAI, download into ComfyUI's `models/loras` folder, see what is installed with its size and trigger word, and delete what you no longer want. - **A GPU whose free memory could not be measured is planned more carefully**, and the log now says total capacity instead of calling it free. - **The Linux AppImage stops handing its own runtime to every program LU starts**, so a healthy system Python, pip, git or ffmpeg keeps working, and a distribution that blocks pip in the system Python keeps the isolated environment LU built. - **The local model runs one conversation at a time and says so**, with a line showing how many chats are ahead. Stop works while a chat is still waiting. - **Temperature, Top P and Max tokens belong to the conversation you moved them in**, instead of every open chat sharing one value. - **Cloud video renders offer the clip lengths the picked model really supports**, read from the live catalog. ## Mobile app (Android, iPhone) LU is also available as an app for your phone. The current APK comes from the 3.0.10 release. - **Android:** download `LU-3.0.10-Android.apk` from the [3.0.10 release](https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored/releases/tag/v3.0.10). Needs Android 7.0 or newer on a 64-bit (arm64) phone. Allow installing apps from your browser or file app when Android asks. SHA-256: `dbd515d81bbc8ab70f21b850424f9f8b57ae88ae24962225beefc4116d139d2f` - **iPhone:** in review at the App Store. - **Google Play:** coming later. What the app does: - Run AI models on your phone and chat offline. Chats with on-device models stay on the phone. - Ask questions about your own documents. Memory and personas. - Optional LU Cloud with your account: larger hosted chat models, Create (images and video) and dictation. - Connect to LU on your own computer over your home Wi-Fi and chat with the models on your PC. Later APKs install over this one and keep your data. The Google Play version will be signed by Google: to switch to it, export your chats first (Settings, Data) and uninstall the APK. ## Three steps 1. **Install.** Run the installer like any other program. On first launch a wizard looks for an AI engine that is already running on your machine, and installs one for you with a single click

readme_content:
# Marketing Skills for AI Agents

A collection of AI agent skills focused on marketing tasks. Built for technical marketers and founders who want AI coding agents to help with conversion optimization, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering. Works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, and any agent that supports the [Agent Skills spec](https://agentskills.io).

Built by [Corey Haines](https://corey.co?ref=marketingskills). Need hands-on help? Check out [Conversion Factory](https://conversionfactory.co?ref=marketingskills) — Corey's agency for conversion optimization, landing pages, and growth strategy. Want to learn more about marketing? Subscribe to [Swipe Files](https://swipefiles.com?ref=marketingskills). Want to get dangerously good at using AI for marketing? Check out [AI Marketing Training](https://conversionfactory.co/offers/ai-marketing-training?ref=marketingskills). Want an autonomous AI agent that uses these skills to be your CMO? Try [Magister](https://magistermarketing.com?ref=marketingskills).

New to the terminal and coding agents? Check out the companion guide [Coding for Marketers](https://codingformarketers.com?ref=marketingskills).

Want your agent to read your marketing accounts? Follow the [guided tool connection workflow](tools/SETUP.md) for scoped credentials and a first read-only result.

**Contributions welcome!** Found a way to improve a skill or have a new one to add? [Open a PR](#contributing).

Run into a problem or have a question? [Open an issue](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills/issues) — we're happy to help.

## Partners

The library is free and MIT-licensed. [Verified Partners](tools/REGISTRY.md#verified-partners) fund the work — vetted, disclosed tool integrations, listed alongside the neutral options and never influencing what the core skills recommend. The full rules and boundaries are in [tools/PARTNERS.md](tools/PARTNERS.md). [Become a partner →](https://marketing-skills.com/sponsorship)

<!-- PARTNERS:START -->
> ◆ **[Converly](https://converly.io)** — *Conversion tracking / attribution.* Server-side conversion tracking that fires when someone submits a form, books a meeting, or starts a chat — passing click IDs and identifiers for Enhanced Conversions (Google) and stronger match quality (Meta), across about 100 tools. CLI + MCP so your agent sets it up in minutes. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/converly.md)

> ◆ **[Ploy](https://ploy.ai)** — *AI website & growth platform.* AI marketing platform built around a hosted website builder — an in-app agent that builds and publishes pages, PloyDB for pages at scale, routing to add pages to an existing site, built-in analytics and visitor identification, and a CLI for coding agents. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/ploy.md)

> ◆ **[AIsa](https://aisa.one)** — *SEO, search & social data.* One AIsa key, pay as you go, instead of a subscription to every data platform. Agents get SEO, search, social, and market data from Similarweb, Semrush, Ahrefs, DataForSEO, Tavily, Reddit, X, and more through REST or MCP, and pay only for the calls they make. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/aisa.md)

> ◆ **[Omnia](https://www.useomnia.com)** — *AI search visibility (AEO).* Omnia tracks how AI engines answer your customers' questions every day: visibility, citations, Share of Voice and sentiment for your brand and competitors. Connect the Omnia MCP to Claude and these skills run on real AI answers data instead of guesses. Or let your Omnia Agent turn it into prioritized work that you review and approve. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/omnia.md)

> ◆ **[Livestorm](https://livestorm.co)** — *Webinars & virtual events.* Browser-based platform for webinars, virtual events, and online meetings, with registration pages, live engagement, recordings, and analytics. A REST API, webhooks, and an official MCP server let agents create events, manage registrants, and pull attendance data. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/livestorm.md)
<!-- PARTNERS:END -->

<!-- The Partners block above is generated from partners.json — run `node scripts/sync-partners.mjs` after editing it. -->

## What are Skills?

Skills are markdown files that give AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows for specific tasks. When you add these to your project, your agent can recognize when you're working on a marketing task and apply the right frameworks and best practices.

## How Skills Work Together

Skills reference each other and build on shared context. The `product-marketing` skill is the foundation — every other skill checks it first to understand your product, audience, and positioning before doing anything.

name: LoopForge
description: Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery. Orchestrate CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates. Includes Local workflows for coding assistants.
readme_content:
English · 简体中文

Two ways to work · Quick start · SOPs · Features · Local · FAQ · Docs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af401d9-1aae-427c-b4bc-455c12d17beb

80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

**LoopForge** is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to **Main Bot** in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an **SOP** (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in. CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code do the work. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license. ## Two ways to work | | **Chat with Main Bot** | **Run an SOP** | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent | Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off | | How it runs | Main Bot opens a [conversation workspace](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents | The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox | | You stay in control by | Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat | Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node | | Delivers | A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch (`mode=direct`) | Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs | Both paths track the same **requirements**, so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

The chat home. Type a request, @ a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

## Why LoopForge Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships. - **Repeatable.** Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. - **Separated roles.** Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat. - **Human in the loop.** Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step. - **Observable and resumable.** Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node. - **Your stack, your servers.** CodeBuddy, Codex or Claude Code as executors. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime. ## Quick start Install **Git** and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set `LOOPFORGE_YES=1` to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git cd LoopForge ./start.sh ``` `./start.sh` pulls the GHCR release image pinned in `compose.yaml` without building locally (`bash scripts/install.sh` does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use `./start.sh logs`, `stop`, `restart` or `pull` to manage it, and `./start.sh dev` to build the checkout from source. If downloads from `ghcr.io` stall, set `MIRROR` to a registry host that can stand in for `ghcr.io`. `./start.sh` pulls from that host and tags the image back to the name pinned in `compose.yaml`. Setting `MIRROR` trusts that host, because the download is tagged with the official name. The GitHub Release records the digest; `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/tencent/loopforge:` should show the same digest after `@`. Without `MIRROR`, `./start.sh` still pulls `ghcr.io` directly, and `compose.yaml` stays unchanged. Upgrade with the same variable and `./start.sh pull`. [ghcr.nju.edu.cn](https://doc.nju.edu.cn/books/e1654/page/ghcr) is one such host. A Docker `registry-mirrors` entry such as `https://docker.nju.edu.cn` only accelerates Docker Hub and is not a value for `MIRROR`. ```bash MIRROR=ghcr.nju.edu.cn ./start.sh ``` Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on `0.0.0.0:8090` by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP. For GitLab, Gitea, Gogs and other Git hosts, [set up Git SSH](docs/deployment.md#git-repositories-over-ssh) to check out and push branches with a personal key. PR/MR and Issue automation requires a hosting API token or a separately configured MCP. ### Try it without an API key New accounts join the **LoopForge demo project**, which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate: 1. Switch to the demo project, open **Templates**, and open **Platform check · script & approval**. 2. Click **Run SOP**. A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step. 3. Approve it from **Needs review** or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact. ### What you need for real work | I want to… | You need | | --- | --- | | Run the script + approval demo | Nothing | | Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new project | An API key for the selected executor | | Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PR | Model credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings) |
More setup details: executors, GitHub, sandboxes, access model
- **Executors.** Pick **CodeBuddy, Codex or Claude Code** beside the home composer, then a model. Each executor uses its own credentials from personal settings, and every SOP role can choose its executor independently (built-in roles default to CodeBuddy). Requirement clarification and AI notification summaries currently use CodeBuddy; scheduled assistant tasks run on the CLI the task selects. The Docker image ships CodeBuddy and Codex; Claude Code installs from npm on first use and is cached, so that first run requires npm access; [native deployments](docs/deployment.md#workers-and-runners) need the CLI for the executor you choose. - **GitHub is optional.** All built-in generic SOPs run without a repository: product SOPs deliver documents, and new frontend/backend projects deliver source files in the task workspace. Bug fixes still need source code and reproduction details. Connect a repository when you work on existing code or want PRs. - **Delivering to a repository.** Choose **Connect GitHub** in personal settings, approve the device code on GitHub and pick your repository (the LoopForge OAuth App is built in; no PAT required, manual PAT entry still works). Set executor credentials (or bind a local execution machine), then either run a project SOP or ask Main Bot to change the code and submit a PR/MR. - **Sandboxes.** In the default Compose installation, SOP runs and conversation workspaces both use Docker sandbox containers started through the host Docker socket. Default sandboxes reuse the installed runtime image, so nothing extra is built after installation; custom Dockerfiles still build their own images. Docker socket access grants control of the host daemon, so this setup is for trusted teams, not untrusted multi-tenant isolation. See [deployment boundaries](docs/deployment.md#accounts). Re-running the installer keeps your data. - **Accounts and access.** New installations listen on all interfaces (existing bind settings are kept) and are designed for a trusted team: signed-in users can read project data across the instance, and teammates can sign up from the login page (`AGENTFLOW_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false` in `.env` turns that off). Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) before exposing it beyond your team. - **Remote access, HTTPS, separate workers.** See [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). - **Hacking on LoopForge itself?** `bash scripts/dev.sh` runs it natively (Go 1.26.11+).
## How SOPs work An **SOP** is the workflow a delivery follows. Agents, scripts and people take part in the same run:

description: Open source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs
readme_content: # OpenSEO > Open source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs OpenSEO is an SEO tool for _the people_. If tools like Semrush or Ahrefs are too expensive or bloated, OpenSEO is a pay-as-you-go alternative that you actually control. > All-in-one SEO tool for you and your AI agent. Connect with any agent like Claude Code, OpenClaw or Hermes. We have pre-built skills, but you can build your own to tailor OpenSEO to your needs. ## Hosted Version Try OpenSEO for free on our website. If you want to support the project, a hosted subscription is $10/month. [openseo.so](https://openseo.so) ### EveryApp Host OpenSEO and other open source apps on our platform EveryApp. [Self-host on EveryApp and give it a star →](https://github.com/every-app/every-app) ## Why use OpenSEO? - Best in class MCP and AI Skills. - Modern, simple UI. - Focused workflows instead of a bloated, complex SEO suite. - No subscriptions. - Bring your own DataForSEO API key and pay only for what you use. - Fork and vibe code your own custom tool. ## Main SEO Workflows - Keyword research - Rank tracking - Competitor Insights - Backlinks - Site Audits - AI Visibility ## OpenSEO MCP & Agent Skills OpenSEO exposes an MCP server so AI agents like Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes can use your SEO data directly. Agent Skills are reusable workflows that guide your agent through SEO tasks using the MCP. - [Set up ChatGPT web or desktop](https://openseo.so/docs/chatgpt) (works on Free and paid ChatGPT plans) - [Set up Codex](https://openseo.so/docs/codex-plugin) - [Set up OpenSEO MCP](https://openseo.so/docs/mcp) - [Set up OpenSEO Agent Skills](https://openseo.so/docs/skills/setup) ## Self-Hosting OpenSEO supports two self-hosting paths. Both use email and password accounts: the first visitor creates the admin account, teammates join from invitation links, and MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor) sign in with the same accounts. - **Docker** - On your own server or computer, with a prebuilt image that is ready in seconds. Works with Compose-based platforms such as Coolify, Portainer and Dokploy. See [`docs/SELF_HOSTING_DOCKER.md`](./docs/SELF_HOSTING_DOCKER.md). - Running the older single-container image? It keeps getting updates; [move to the new setup](./docs/SELF_HOSTING_DOCKER.md#move-from-the-old-docker-image) when you are ready, data included. - **Cloudflare** - No server to run: one deploy command puts OpenSEO on your own Cloudflare account (works on the free plan). See [`docs/SELF_HOSTING_CLOUDFLARE.md`](./docs/SELF_HOSTING_CLOUDFLARE.md). For security-conscious setups, two advanced options replace the accounts with your own network controls: - **Cloudflare Access** in front of the Cloudflare deploy, so Cloudflare checks every request before it reaches OpenSEO. See [`docs/SELF_HOSTING_CLOUDFLARE.md`](./docs/SELF_HOSTING_CLOUDFLARE.md). - **No sign-in on Docker**, behind Tailscale, a private network or your own authenticating proxy. See [Without sign-in](./docs/SELF_HOSTING_DOCKER.md#without-sign-in-advanced). Either way, you need a DataForSEO API key to get SEO data. See [`docs/DATAFORSEO_API_KEY.md`](./docs/DATAFORSEO_API_KEY.md). ## Costs OpenSEO needs a [DataForSEO](https://dataforseo.com/?aff=255379) API key so that you can get SEO data. You pay them directly when self hosting. See [openseo.so/pricing](https://openseo.so/pricing) When you self host, your costs will be slightly lower than the estimates on our website. The way the hosted service makes money is by charging 28% extra for every request we make to DataForSEO. ## Local Development See [`docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md`](./docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md). ## Contributing Creating clear issues is the best way to contribute. Read more here: [`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`](./.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) We have this skill: `/simple-issue-description` which helps. ```sh npx skills add every-app/open-seo --skill simple-issue-description ``` ## Community Join Discord to chat: [Discord](https://discord.gg/c9uGs3cFXr) Follow along for updates: - Follow on X: https://x.com/bensenescu - Sign up for the mailing list on our website: [openseo.so](https://openseo.so)

readme_content:
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@qwen-code/qwen-code.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@qwen-code/qwen-code) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/QwenLM/qwen-code.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Node.js Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.0.0-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org/) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@qwen-code/qwen-code.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@qwen-code/qwen-code) **The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat.** 中文 | Deutsch | français | 日本語 | Русский | Português (Brasil) | 한국어
![Qwen Code in the terminal, desktop app, browser, editor, and chat, with VS Code, Zed, JetBrains, Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, and Feishu integrations](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i1/O1CN01DXWdF8BDUdD3XPhl_!!6000000001721-2-tps-1743-902.png) | **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview** | | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Qwen Code 1.0 Preview brings together the agent harness capabilities of [Qoder](https://qoder.com/) and Qwen Code in an open-source release.

[Try Qwen Code 1.0 Preview](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview) · [Documentation](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/) · [中文文档](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/zh/users/overview/). | ## Why Qwen Code? - **Agentic out of the box** — Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams, and MCP. Dynamic workflows, zero setup. - **Open-source, inside and out** — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in. - **Multi-protocol** — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. - **Beyond the terminal** — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / Feishu). > [!TIP] > Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI. ## Installation Looking for **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview**? [Get started here](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview). The instructions below are for the main version. **Linux / macOS:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash ``` **Windows:** ```powershell irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex ``` > Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect.
NPM / Homebrew **NPM** (requires [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org/)): ```bash npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest ``` **Homebrew** (macOS / Linux): ```bash brew install qwen-code ```
## Quick Start Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code: ```bash cd /path/to/your-project qwen ``` Inside the session, run `/auth` and choose [**Qwen Account with Subscription**](https://chat.qwen.ai/?memberPlan=qwen_code&entry=qwen_code&paywallScene=cli) to sign in with your **Plus or Pro subscription**, or configure a provider with an API key. Then try: ```text Explain this repository and show me where to start. ``` See the [Authentication Guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/) and [Settings Reference](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/settings/) for detailed setup.
See the terminal interface ![Qwen Code terminal interface](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i2/O1CN01K0nwj41RM1Il8kB0t_!!6000000002096-2-tps-1544-1060.png)
## How to Use Qwen Code Choose the interface that fits your workflow: | Interface | Get started | | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Terminal** | Run `qwen` in your project — see [Quick Start](#quick-start). | | **Desktop** | [Download Qwen Code Desktop](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/tag/desktop-latest) for macOS, Windows, and Linux. | | **Web** | Run `qwen serve --open` to open the [Web UI](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/) in your browser. _(experimental)_ | | **Editor** | Set up [VS Code](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-vscode/), [Zed](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-zed/), or [JetBrains](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-jetbrains/). | | **Chat** | Connect [Telegram](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/telegram/), [DingTalk](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/dingtalk/), [WeChat](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/weixin/), or [Feishu](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/feishu/), then run `qwen channel start`. | For automation and custom integrations: - **Headless** — Run `qwen -p "..."` in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs. - **SDKs** — Build with [TypeScript](./packages/sdk-typescript/README.md), [Python](./packages/sdk-python/README.md), or [Java](./packages/sdk-java/qwencode/README.md). - **Daemon** — Run `qwen serve` to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). _(experimental)_ [Daemon guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/). - **Computer Use** — Set up [native MCP tools](./packages/cua-driver/README.md#agent-integration) or [Node REPL + SDK](./packages/node-repl/README.md#usage) in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex.
SDK example (Python) ```python import asyncio from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query async def main() -> None: result = query( "Summarize the repository layout.", { "cwd": "/path/to/project", "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen", }, ) async for message in result: if is_sdk_result_message(message): print(message["result"]) asyncio.run(main()) ```
## Daemon Mode Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions. Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell: ```bash qwen serve --open ``` The default address is `http://127.0.0.1:4170`. To run and manage it in the background instead: ```bash qwen daemon start qwen daemon status qwen daemon logs -f qwen daemon stop ``` By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` and use `--require-auth`. See the [Daemon guide](./docs/users/qwen-serve.md) for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API. ## Capabilities If you know Claude Code, you already know Qwen Code — and then some. We've put significant effort into [bringing Qwen Code to feature parity with Claude Code](https://github.com/wenshao/codeagents/blob/main/docs/comparison/qwen-code-improvement-report.md), improving both breadth and reliability across the board. | Feature | Qwen Code | Claude Code | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | :-------: | :---------: | | SubAgents, Agent Teams, Dynamic Workflows | ✓ | ✓ | | Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, Hooks | ✓ | ✓ | | Built-in Skills (/review, /batch, /loop, /bugfix…) | ✓ | ✓ | | MCP, Plan Mode, LSP Integration | ✓ | ✓ | | Auto Mode, Sandbox, Git Worktrees | ✓ | ✓ | | Computer Use (desktop automation) | ✓ | ✓ | | IDE Plugins (VS Code / JetBrains / Zed) | ✓ | ✓ | | SDK | ✓ | ✓ | | Headless Mode, Session Management | ✓ | ✓ | | Open-source — model and framework | ✓ | — | | Multi-protocol (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Qwen + any provider) | ✓ | — | | Agent Arena (multi-model head-to-head on same task) | ✓ | — | | Daemon Mode — `qwen serve` (multi-client shared agent) | ✓ | — | | IM Channels (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat
