readme_content:
# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) before it writes any code. ## Contributing with agents Please use [Agent Traffic Control](https://github.com/ashhart/ATC) before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes. Check the [live agent radar](https://tensorfold.dev/atc) before choosing an issue and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [ATC contributor instructions](docs/atc/SKILL.md). Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone: ```sh npm install -g github:ashhart/ATC atc check ISSUE --json atc claim ISSUE --json ``` Replace `ISSUE` with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free. TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its `session` number. Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session. For work already yours, start a session with `atc start ISSUE --json`. Add `--github-name` to `claim` or `start` only if you want your verified GitHub name shown; `--local` keeps a new session on your machine. The board shows the issue, activity state and last check-in; GitHub still associates the verification comment with its author. Check that `publication` is `public`; `unavailable` means the public update failed even if the local claim or session succeeded. Pulse only while the agent is working, before its five-minute check-in expires: ```sh atc pulse ISSUE SESSION working --json atc who path/to/file --json atc overlap --json atc land ISSUE SESSION --json atc release ISSUE --json ``` Use `reviewing` or `blocked` when appropriate, land the session when it stops, and resolve overlaps before opening a pull request. Before opening a pull request, have the agent run the [pull request skill](docs/pr/SKILL.md); agents that support skills can install it as `tensorfold-pull-request`. ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, the small 4-bit checkpoint checked on Metal and a GB10. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. Reviewing or benchmarking TensorFold? [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) covers pinning, signature checks, a container and the tests that need no GPU. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Use the release archive for your CPU: `linux-aarch64` on a GB10, `linux-x86_64` on an x86_64 host. It needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0), providing `libcuda.so.1`. Keep the archive's directories together. Its kernels are built with CUDA 13, so TensorFold refuses an older driver at startup; `nvidia-smi` shows the installed one. See the [CUDA runbook](RUNBOOK.md#linux-and-cuda) for runtime libraries and supported GPUs. ```sh V=1.2.7 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. On Windows with an NVIDIA GPU, follow [the native Windows build guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). Use `tensorfold --help`, `tensorfold capabilities --json` and `tensorfold serve REPO --help` to inspect your binary. You can also serve a complete local checkpoint directory or an existing Hugging Face cache. `tensorfold web [ARGS...]` opens TensorFold Web, a small local web app for picking, running and chatting with models. If it needs installing, an interactive release binary offers to install its matching version with `uv` after you say yes. See [the web launcher](docs/web.md) for manual installation and unattended use. `--parallel N` caps active requests at N; extra requests wait for a free slot. Omitting the flag uses `--parallel auto`, which asks for up to eight streams as memory and the engine allow. An explicit number is refused if the engine cannot fit that many streams. Read the engine's startup capacity line, such as `8 streams at once` on CUDA, for the count it accepted. With API authentication off, `/health` reports `live.connections` as active plus waiting requests and `live.waiting` as the queued count. For example, 8 connections with 4 waiting means 4 active requests. Completing or cancelling an active request frees its slot; cancelling a waiting request removes it from the queue. ## Mac app The [TensorFold desktop workspace](app/README.md) bundles the local engine, model downloads, hardware recommendations, live generation metrics, coding workers and document editing. Download the Apple-silicon [beta 9 DMG](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/tag/v1.0.0-beta.9), or build from [`app/`](app/README.md). The desktop app launches the bundled `tensorfold-native` executable directly. Mobile clients in `app/mobile/` remain preview software. ## TensorFold Starlight (enterprise) [TensorFold Starlight](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight) gives an organisation one governed OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoint for a fleet of TensorFold engines on Macs, Linux GPU servers and Windows machines. It signs people in through the organisation's identity provider (OIDC or SAML, with SCIM provisioning), decides who may use which model and where it runs, places and supervises models on nodes, and accounts for every token. It runs fully offline, or brokers approved frontier providers under the same identity, policy and budgets; [the install guide](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight/blob/main/docs/install.md) covers Docker, Kubernetes and Linux services. Starlight lives in its own repository, [ashhart/tf-starlight](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight): it pins the TensorFold release it is tested with and checks every flag its nodes pass to `tensorfold serve` against that release in CI. Starlight is new: the gates that still need real GPU clusters or identity-provider tenants are listed in [its qualification notes](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight/blob/main/docs/qualification.md). ## Living Weights (experimental) Living Weights teaches a running model new facts in its own weights. Start a Nemotron 3.5 Lightning server with `--slide` and tell it something: each fact that passes the lesson's checks is written into the checkpoint folder's files. It is experimental: related facts can disturb each other, recall drops past a few dozen facts and with thinking on, and learned facts cost some decode speed on a Mac. [Known issues](docs/known-issues.md#living-weights---slide) has the details. ```sh tensorfold pull TensorFold/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit hub="${HF_HUB_CACHE:-${HF_HOME:-$HOME/.cache/huggingface}/hub}/models--TensorFold--NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit" src="$hub/snapshots/$(cat "$hub/refs/main")" mkdir -p ~/models && cp -RL "$src" ~/models/nemotron-living # always teach a copy (umask 077; openssl rand -hex 24 > ~/models/slide-key) # --slide starts only with a key tensorfold serve ~/models/nemotron-living --slide --api-key-file ~/models/slide-key ``` Leave that server running and send a lesson from another terminal: ```sh curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/slide/learn -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/models/slide-key)" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text": "I like blue."}' ``` Send it a document instead and it finds the facts in it and learns them one by one. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/slide` to watch in 3D: the facts, the neurons each one took in the model's layers, the shard files that hold them, and the lesson running now. Learning runs on Apple-silicon Macs and on an NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), and a folder that learned on one serves on the other. On an APFS volume, `cp -cRL` makes a clone that shares the original's data until lessons change it. It rewrites the folder's files: before the first lesson the server keeps the originals in a hidden snapshot, and `tensorfold slide rollback ~/models/nemotron-living` puts them back, undoing every lesson. The [Living Weights guide](docs/living-weights.md) covers the key, teaching files and web pages, omp's `/learn` command, the 3D view, undoing lessons, and what to expect. ## Pick a model These are the native release's serving paths. A recipe may also describe the older Python 0.6.6 engine; use its native section and the current [changes](CHANGELOG.md) together. Hardware below records the documented scope, not an unmeasured minimum. Context, parallel requests, prompt caches and drafters need memory beyond the weights. `tensorfold info REPO` reports the checkpoint's memory floor. Where no RAM capacity is published, inspect that floor before serving a large checkpoint. CUDA release images include sm_80, sm_86, sm_120 and sm_121. The A100 (sm_80) has kernel-check evidence ([#846](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/846)), but no served checkpoint on record, so it is not model-qualified. Nemotron and dense Qwen have NVFP4/FP8 fallback code for sm_80 to sm_89 (#901, #1470); no such model run on sm_80 to sm_89 is recorded. Run a table command after installation. On a Linux archive installation, use the `tensorfold` shell function from Quick start. `REPO@revision` pins a pull; serve the repository name without the revision after pulling it. Conversions are explicitly marked: their upstream weights need the linked conversion before native serving. | Model / format | Download | Machine and memory scope | Native recipe / limits | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | dots.mocr, BF16 OCR | Use the local `dots-studio/dots.mocr` checkpoint. | Native HIP; AMD R9700 (`gfx1201`) checked, one GPU. | [Native OCR recipe](docs/recipes/dots-mocr-hip.md); full model-card demo matches HF tokens. Native CUDA serves text prompts only ([CUDA recipe](docs/recipes/dots-mocr-cuda.md)). No video, MTP head, or Metal qualification. | | Qwen3.5-2B, MLX 4-bit | `tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3` | One Mac (M5 Max checked), or one GB10; no RAM minimum published. | [2B](docs/recipes/qwen3.5-2b-native.md); [CUDA release checks](CHANGELOG.md#110). Text only. | | Qwen3.8-27B, MLX 4-bit | `tensorfold pull TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit`
`tensorfold pull z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` | One Mac (M5 Max/M3 Ultra), or one GB10; a 32 GB Mac needs `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` raised (the startup refusal names the value). | [27B](docs/recipes/qwen3.8-27b.md). Add `--drafter z-lab/Qwen3

readme_content:
# [React](https://react.dev/) · [![GitHub license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/react/react/blob/main/LICENSE) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/react.svg?style=flat)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react) [![(Runtime) Build and Test](https://github.com/react/react/actions/workflows/runtime_build_and_test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/react/react/actions/workflows/runtime_build_and_test.yml) [![(Compiler) TypeScript](https://github.com/react/react/actions/workflows/compiler_typescript.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/react/react/actions/workflows/compiler_typescript.yml) [![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/how-to-contribute.html#your-first-pull-request) React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. * **Declarative:** React makes it painless to create interactive UIs. Design simple views for each state in your application, and React will efficiently update and render just the right components when your data changes. Declarative views make your code more predictable, simpler to understand, and easier to debug. * **Component-Based:** Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs. Since component logic is written in JavaScript instead of templates, you can easily pass rich data through your app and keep the state out of the DOM. * **Learn Once, Write Anywhere:** We don't make assumptions about the rest of your technology stack, so you can develop new features in React without rewriting existing code. React can also render on the server using [Node](https://nodejs.org/en) and power mobile apps using [React Native](https://reactnative.dev/). [Learn how to use React in your project](https://react.dev/learn). ## Installation React has been designed for gradual adoption from the start, and **you can use as little or as much React as you need**: * Use [Quick Start](https://react.dev/learn) to get a taste of React. * [Add React to an Existing Project](https://react.dev/learn/add-react-to-an-existing-project) to use as little or as much React as you need. * [Create a New React App](https://react.dev/learn/start-a-new-react-project) if you're looking for a powerful JavaScript toolchain. ## Documentation You can find the React documentation [on the website](https://react.dev/). Check out the [Getting Started](https://react.dev/learn) page for a quick overview. The documentation is divided into several sections: * [Quick Start](https://react.dev/learn) * [Tutorial](https://react.dev/learn/tutorial-tic-tac-toe) * [Thinking in React](https://react.dev/learn/thinking-in-react) * [Installation](https://react.dev/learn/installation) * [Describing the UI](https://react.dev/learn/describing-the-ui) * [Adding Interactivity](https://react.dev/learn/adding-interactivity) * [Managing State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) * [Advanced Guides](https://react.dev/learn/escape-hatches) * [API Reference](https://react.dev/reference/react) * [Where to Get Support](https://react.dev/community) * [Contributing Guide](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/how-to-contribute.html) You can improve it by sending pull requests to [this repository](https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev). ## Examples We have several examples [on the website](https://react.dev/). Here is the first one to get you started: ```jsx import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'; function HelloMessage({ name }) { return
Hello {name}
; } const root = createRoot(document.getElementById('container')); root.render(); ``` This example will render "Hello Taylor" into a container on the page. You'll notice that we used an HTML-like syntax; [we call it JSX](https://react.dev/learn#writing-markup-with-jsx). JSX is not required to use React, but it makes code more readable, and writing it feels like writing HTML. ## Contributing The main purpose of this repository is to continue evolving React core, making it faster and easier to use. Development of React happens in the open on GitHub, and we are grateful to the community for contributing bugfixes and improvements. Read below to learn how you can take part in improving React. ### [Code of Conduct](https://code.fb.com/codeofconduct) Facebook has adopted a Code of Conduct that we expect project participants to adhere to. Please read [the full text](https://code.fb.com/codeofconduct) so that you can understand what actions will and will not be tolerated. ### [Contributing Guide](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/how-to-contribute.html) Read our [contributing guide](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/how-to-contribute.html) to learn about our development process, how to propose bugfixes and improvements, and how to build and test your changes to React. ### [Good First Issues](https://github.com/react/react/labels/good%20first%20issue) To help you get your feet wet and get you familiar with our contribution process, we have a list of [good first issues](https://github.com/react/react/labels/good%20first%20issue) that contain bugs that have a relatively limited scope. This is a great place to get started. ### License React is [MIT licensed](./LICENSE).

readme_content:
Claude Code Templates

An open catalog of components for Claude Code, installable with one command.

Browse the catalog  ·  Documentation  ·  Contributing  ·  Discussions  ·  Changelog

SPONSORED BY

Swiftproxy proudly supports this project.
Connect your AI-powered workflows to reliable residential proxies for web data collection, browser automation, and AI-driven research.
90M+ residential IPs across 220+ locations, rotating and static residential proxies, with HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 support.

## About Claude Code is configured through small files: skills, subagents, slash commands, hooks, MCP servers and settings. Claude Code Templates collects more than 1,980 of them in one catalog at [aitmpl.com](https://www.aitmpl.com), where you can search, preview every file a component writes, and combine several components into a single install command. The CLI writes each file to the right place and merges existing configuration instead of overwriting it. Every pull request is checked by Claude Code's plugin validator and scanned by [NVIDIA SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector). ## Quickstart Runs with `npx`, no global install needed. ```bash # Browse the catalog and install interactively npx claude-code-templates@latest # Install one component npx claude-code-templates@latest --skill creative-design/frontend-design # Install a stack in one command npx claude-code-templates@latest \ --agent development-team/frontend-developer \ --command testing/generate-tests \ --mcp integration/github-integration ``` Add `--yes` to skip the confirmation prompt. Every component page on [aitmpl.com](https://www.aitmpl.com) shows its exact install command. To find one from the terminal: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --search "code review"`.
One example per component type ```bash npx claude-code-templates@latest --skill creative-design/frontend-design npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent development-tools/code-reviewer npx claude-code-templates@latest --command performance/optimize-bundle-size npx claude-code-templates@latest --mcp database/postgresql-integration npx claude-code-templates@latest --setting mcp/mcp-timeouts npx claude-code-templates@latest --hook git/conventional-commits npx claude-code-templates@latest --mod security/secret-redactor # Claude Code 2.1.287+ npx claude-code-templates@latest --loop engineering/docs-sweep-loop # also installs the components the loop uses npx claude-code-templates@latest --plugin productivity/champion-kit # via the aitmpl marketplace, Claude Code 2.1.288+ ```
## What's in the catalog | Type | Count | What it is | Examples | |------|------:|------------|----------| | **Skills** | 918 | Reusable capabilities with progressive disclosure | PDF processing, frontend design, code review | | **Agents** | 422 | Subagents specialized in one domain | Security auditor, frontend developer, database architect | | **Commands** | 288 | Custom slash commands | `/generate-tests`, `/optimize-bundle-size`, `/security-audit` | | **MCPs** | 119 | External service integrations | GitHub, PostgreSQL, Stripe, Supabase, Sentry | | **Settings** | 80 | Claude Code configuration | Timeouts, permissions, status lines | | **Hooks** | 63 | Automation triggers | Conventional commits, blocking direct pushes | | **Mods** | 50 | Plugins that change Claude Code's own interface and behavior | Secret redaction, protected paths, terminal games | | **Loops** | 18 | Autonomous workflows with a goal, an interval and a stop condition | Docs sweep, build-test-fix, adversarial review | | **Templates** | 14 | Complete project configurations | Language and framework setups | | **Sandboxes** | 11 | Launchers that run Claude Code in an isolated environment (reference only, see [`cli-tool/components/sandbox/`](cli-tool/components/sandbox/)) | E2B, Cloudflare, Docker | | **Plugins** | 1 | Whole Claude Code plugins, installed from the `aitmpl` marketplace | Champion Kit | Live counts: [`dashboard/public/counts.json`](dashboard/public/counts.json). ## Local tools The CLI also ships three local tools. The two dashboards listen on `127.0.0.1` only, because they serve your conversation history. | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `npx claude-code-templates@latest --analytics` | Real-time session monitoring and usage metrics at `localhost:3333` | | `npx claude-code-templates@latest --chats` | Read and search your conversations in a mobile-friendly UI at `localhost:9876` | | `npx claude-code-templates@latest --health-check` | Diagnose your Claude Code installation and project setup | To open the conversation browser from another device, forward the port over SSH: `ssh -L 9876:localhost:9876 `.
Flags removed in 1.31.0 `--plugins`, `--skills-manager`, `--command-stats`, `--hook-stats`, `--mcp-stats`, `--agents`, `--chats-mobile`, `--teams`, `--2025`, `--studio`, `--sandbox`, `--tunnel`, `--create-agent`, `--list-agents`, `--update-agent`, `--remove-agent` and `--clone-session` were removed. Running one prints what replaced it. To see what is installed in each scope, use the [stack viewer mod](https://www.aitmpl.com/component/mods/ui/stack-viewer) (`--mod ui/stack-viewer`, then `/stack` in Claude Code). Details in the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md).
## Documentation Guides, the CLI reference and the catalog API live at **[docs.aitmpl.com](https://docs.aitmpl.com)**. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Read the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) to add a skill, agent, command, MCP, setting, hook or mod, and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before you open a pull request. ## Sponsors and programs ### Sponsors

name: tauri
description: Build smaller, faster, and more secure desktop and mobile applications with a web frontend.
readme_content:
[![status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-stable-blue.svg)](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/tree/dev) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT%20or%20Apache%202-green.svg)](https://opencollective.com/tauri) [![test core](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tauri-apps/tauri/test-core.yml?label=test%20core&logo=github)](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/actions/workflows/test-core.yml) [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Ftauri-apps%2Ftauri.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Ftauri-apps%2Ftauri?ref=badge_shield) [![Chat Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-discord-7289da.svg)](https://discord.com/invite/tauri) [![website](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-tauri.app-purple.svg)](https://tauri.app) [![https://good-labs.github.io/greater-good-affirmation/assets/images/badge.svg](https://good-labs.github.io/greater-good-affirmation/assets/images/badge.svg)](https://good-labs.github.io/greater-good-affirmation) [![support](https://img.shields.io/badge/sponsor-Open%20Collective-blue.svg)](https://opencollective.com/tauri) ## Introduction Tauri is a framework for building tiny, blazingly fast binaries for all major operating systems. Developers can integrate any front-end framework that compiles to HTML, JS and CSS for building their user interface. The backend of the application is a rust-sourced binary with an API that the front-end can interact with. The user interface in Tauri apps currently leverages [`tao`](https://docs.rs/tao) as a window handling library on macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS. To render your application, Tauri uses [WRY](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry), a library which provides a unified interface to the system webview, leveraging WKWebView on macOS & iOS, WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on Linux and Android System WebView on Android. To learn more about the details of how all of these pieces fit together, please consult this [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md) document. ## Getting Started If you are interested in making a tauri app, please visit the [documentation website](https://tauri.app). The quickest way to get started is to install the [prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) for your system and create a new project with [`create-tauri-app`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/create-tauri-app/#usage). For example with `npm`: ```sh npm create tauri-app@latest ``` ## Features The list of Tauri's features includes, but is not limited to: - Built-in app bundler to create app bundles in formats like `.app`, `.dmg`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` and Windows installers like `.exe` (via NSIS) and `.msi` (via WiX). - Built-in self updater (desktop only) - System tray icons - Native notifications - Native WebView Protocol (tauri doesn't create a localhost http(s) server to serve the WebView contents) - GitHub action for streamlined CI - VS Code extension ### Platforms Tauri currently supports development and distribution on the following platforms: | Platform | Versions | | :--------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Windows | 10 and above | | macOS | 10.15 and above | | Linux | webkit2gtk 4.0 for Tauri v1 (for example Ubuntu 18.04). webkit2gtk 4.1 for Tauri v2 (for example Ubuntu 22.04). | | iOS/iPadOS | 9 and above | | Android | 7 and above (currently 8 and above) | ## Contributing Before you start working on something, it's best to check if there is an existing issue first. It's also a good idea to stop by the Discord server and confirm with the team if it makes sense or if someone else is already working on it. Please make sure to read the [Contributing Guide](./.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) before making a pull request. Thank you to everyone contributing to Tauri! ### Documentation Documentation in a polyglot system is a tricky proposition. To this end, we prefer to use inline documentation in the Rust & JS source code as much as possible. Check out the hosting repository for the documentation site for further information: ## Partners
For the complete list of sponsors please visit our [website](https://tauri.app#sponsors) and [Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/tauri). ## Organization Tauri aims to be a sustainable collective based on principles that guide sustainable free and open software communities. To this end it has become a Programme within the [Commons Conservancy](https://commonsconservancy.org/), and you can contribute financially via [Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/tauri). ## Licenses Code: (c) 2015 - Present - The Tauri Programme within The Commons Conservancy. MIT or MIT/Apache 2.0 where applicable. Logo: CC-BY-NC-ND - Original Tauri Logo Designs by [Alve Larsson](https://alve.io/), [Daniel Thompson-Yvetot](https://github.com/nothingismagick) and [Guillaume Chau](https://github.com/akryum) [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Ftauri-apps%2Ftauri.svg?type=large)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Ftauri-apps%2Ftauri?ref=badge_large)

name: fastapi
description: FastAPI framework, high performance, easy to learn, fast to code, ready for production
readme_content:
FastAPI framework, high performance, easy to learn, fast to code, ready for production

--- **Documentation**: [https://fastapi.tiangolo.com](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com) **Source Code**: [https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi) --- FastAPI is a modern, fast (high-performance), web framework for building APIs with Python based on standard Python type hints. The key features are: * **Fast**: Very high performance, on par with **NodeJS** and **Go** (thanks to Starlette and Pydantic). [One of the fastest Python frameworks available](#performance). * **Fast to code**: Increase the speed to develop features by about 200% to 300%. * * **Fewer bugs**: Reduce about 40% of human (developer) induced errors. * * **Intuitive**: Great editor support. Completion everywhere. Less time debugging. * **Easy**: Designed to be easy to use and learn. Less time reading docs. * **Short**: Minimize code duplication. Multiple features from each parameter declaration. Fewer bugs. * **Robust**: Get production-ready code. With automatic interactive documentation. * **Standards-based**: Based on (and fully compatible with) the open standards for APIs: [OpenAPI](https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification) (previously known as Swagger) and [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/). * estimation based on tests conducted by an internal development team, building production applications. ## Sponsors ### Keystone Sponsor ### Gold Sponsors ### Silver Sponsors [Other sponsors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/fastapi-people/#sponsors) ## Opinions
"_[...] I'm using **FastAPI** a ton these days. [...] I'm actually planning to use it for all of my team's **ML services at Microsoft**. Some of them are getting integrated into the core **Windows** product and some **Office** products._"
Kabir Khan - Microsoft (ref)
--- "_We adopted the **FastAPI** library to spawn a **REST** server that can be queried to obtain **predictions**. [for Ludwig]_"
Piero Molino, Yaroslav Dudin, and Sai Sumanth Miryala - Uber (ref)
--- "_**Netflix** is pleased to announce the open-source release of our **crisis management** orchestration framework: **Dispatch**! [built with **FastAPI**]_"
Kevin Glisson, Marc Vilanova, Forest Monsen - Netflix (ref)
--- "_If anyone is looking to build a production Python API, I would highly recommend **FastAPI**. It is **beautifully designed**, **simple to use** and **highly scalable**, it has become a **key component** in our API first development strategy and is driving many automations and services such as our Virtual TAC Engineer._"
Deon Pillsbury - Cisco (ref)
---
## FastAPI mini documentary There's a [FastAPI mini documentary](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpR8ngthqiE) released at the end of 2025, you can watch it online: ## **Typer**, the FastAPI of CLIs If you are building a CLI app to be used in the terminal instead of a web API, check out [**Typer**](https://typer.tiangolo.com/). **Typer** is FastAPI's little sibling. And it's intended to be the **FastAPI of CLIs**. ⌨️ 🚀 ## Requirements FastAPI stands on the shoulders of giants: * [Starlette](https://starlette.dev/) for the web parts. * [Pydantic](https://pydantic.dev/docs/) for the data parts. ## Installation First, [install `uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), and then add FastAPI to your project:
```console $ uv add "fastapi[standard]" ---> 100% ```
**Note**: Make sure you put `"fastapi[standard]"` in quotes to ensure it works in all terminals. If you prefer to use `pip`, install `fastapi[standard]` inside a virtual environment. See the [installation guide](tutorial/#install-fastapi) for the alternative steps. ## Example ### Create it Create a file `main.py` with: ```Python from fastapi import FastAPI app = FastAPI() @app.get("/") def read_root(): return {"Hello": "World"} @app.get("/items/{item_id}") def read_item(item_id: int, q: str | None = None): return {"item_id": item_id, "q": q} ```
Or use async def... If your code uses `async` / `await`, use `async def`: ```Python hl_lines="7 12" from fastapi import FastAPI app = FastAPI() @app.get("/") async def read_root(): return {"Hello": "World"} @app.get("/items/{item_id}") async def read_item(item_id: int, q: str | None = None): return {"item_id": item_id, "q": q} ``` **Note**: If you don't know, check the _"In a hurry?"_ section about [`async` and `await` in the docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/async/#in-a-hurry).
### Run it Run the server with:
```console $ uv run fastapi dev ╭────────── FastAPI CLI - Development mode ───────────╮ │ │ │ Serving at: http://127.0.0.1:8000 │ │ │ │ API docs: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs │ │ │ │ Running in development mode, for production use: │ │ │ │ fastapi run │ │ │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ INFO: Will watch for changes in these directories: ['/home/user/code/awesomeapp'] INFO: Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit) INFO: Started reloader process [2248755] using WatchFiles INFO: Started server process [2248757] INFO: Waiting for application startup. INFO: Application startup complete. ```
About the command fastapi dev... The command `fastapi dev` reads your `main.py` file automatically, detects the **FastAPI** app in it, and starts a server using [Uvicorn](https://uvicorn.dev). By default, `fastapi dev` will start with auto-reload enabled for local development. You can read more about it in the [FastAPI CLI docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/fastapi-cli/).
### Check it Open your browser at [http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/5?q=somequery](http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/5?q=somequery). You will see the JSON response as: ```JSON {"item_id": 5, "q": "somequery"} ``` You already created an API that: * Receives HTTP requests in the _paths_ `/` and `/items/{item_id}`. * Both _paths_ take `GET` operations (also known as HTTP _methods_). * The _path_ `/items/{it

name: SkillEvaluator
description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills with quality gates, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior.
readme_content:
# SkillEvaluator

![SkillEvaluator wordmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/skillevaluator-wordmark.svg)

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%20%7C%203.13%20%7C%203.14-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Documentation-docs.nvidia.com-blue.svg)](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/)
[![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2608.20614-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614)
[![NVIDIA Developer Blog](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blog-NVIDIA%20Developer-76B900.svg)](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/)

> 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI)

SkillEvaluator is an open-source tool that checks AI agent skills and measures their effect on task results:
start with quality checks, then compare live runs with and without a skill.

Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the
[Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of
the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills).

## Bring skill evaluation to your repository

Check changed skills in GitHub or GitLab with quality checks, SkillSpector
security scanning and reports. Choose folders and thresholds; no evaluator code
to import.

**GitHub guided setup:** run inside your checked-out repository:

```bash
pip install --upgrade skillevaluator
skillevaluator ci init
```

Choose checks and optional hosted feedback, then review the setup PR.
[CLI setup guide](docs/cli-onboarding.mdx).

**Manual setup:** copy a filled-in template from
[CI templates](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/tree/main/ci/bundles/0.8.0). No local CLI needed.

| Your repository | Ready-to-use template | Copy destination |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | [Skill checks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/0.8.0/skill-checks.yml) | `.github/workflows/skill-checks.yml` |
| GitLab | [Skill checks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/0.8.0/gitlab-skill-checks.yml) | `.gitlab-ci.yml`, or merge into your existing pipeline |
| GitHub reports and PR comments | [Optional publisher](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/ci/bundles/0.8.0/publish-skill-reports.yml) | Second workflow; complete publisher setup |

See [GitHub](docs/github-actions.mdx) and [GitLab](docs/gitlab-ci.mdx) setup,
[template reference](ci/templates/README.md) and [report examples](ci/examples/README.md).

## Quickstart

Both paths use the bundled `text-analyzer` skill.

| Start here | Requires | First result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Run without an LLM](#run-without-an-llm) | Git and uv | A deterministic quality score and findings |
| [Use NVIDIA Build](#use-nvidia-build) | Git, uv, and a Build API key | Model-backed rubric scores and feedback |

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git,
then get the example:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git
cd SkillEvaluator
```

uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies. Run from this checkout; for a standalone CLI, see
[Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation).

### Run without an LLM

```bash
uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \
  src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \
  -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality
```

No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores **84.5/100 (B)**,
exits `0` and saves `reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json`. The
passing threshold defaults to 70.

This checks static quality; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security
needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path
with your skill directory. See the
[keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm).

### Use NVIDIA Build

Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for
**free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product).

1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment.
2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key.
3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check:

```bash
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build
export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...'
uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \
  src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \
  -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build
```

The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in
`reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json`. No agent runtime or Docker is
needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds.

The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the
[Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) or [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx).

## Three-tier overview

![SkillEvaluator three-tier pipeline: Skill → Tier 1 Validation → Tier 2 Deduplication → Tier 3 Live Evaluation → Reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/three-tier-overview.svg)

Each tier is independent. Add the relevant extra to your checkout command:

| Tier | Question | Example after setup | Additional setup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1: Validation | Is the skill safe and well-formed? | `uv run --extra security skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm` | External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks |
| Tier 2: Deduplication | Does guidance repeat or overlap? | `uv run --extra tier2 skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill` | Embeddings and chat; add `--catalog ./skill-catalog.json` for inter-skill comparison |
| Tier 3: Live Evaluation | Does the skill help the agent? | `uv run --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill` | Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default) |

Tier 1 fetches pinned, verified SkillSpector and Gitleaks releases when they
are missing; Semgrep is optional. See [scanners](docs/installation.mdx#system-tools).
`--no-llm` does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is
`INCOMPLETE` and exits nonzero.
[SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) provides specialized skill
security scanning; [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor), the
open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs.

Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 reuses evaluation
sources or creates one starter case with limited coverage. See the
[tier guides](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) for details.

## Run the combined pipeline

After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers:

```bash
uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker
uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator validate ./my-skill
```

`doctor` checks readiness, not inference success. `validate` runs all tiers with
autopilot for skills. Use `--tiers 1,2` to skip live evaluation or `--tiers 1` for
static checks. `--no-autopilot` requires an existing source. Other artifact types
retain their applicable stages.

Tier 1 always gates `validate`. Tier 2 gates unless `--no-block-on-dedup` is set;
Tier 3 gates only with `--block-on-agent-eval`. Model and managed-sandbox usage
can incur charges; see [runtime and cost](docs/tier3-live-evaluation.mdx#plan-for-cost).

For broader coverage, generate and review additional cases. Templates omit
negatives unless authored in `EVAL.md`:

```bash
uv run --python 3.13 --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full
```

## Run from a source checkout

Use `uv run --python 3.13` with the relevant extra. See
[Installation](docs/installation.mdx#choosing-extras) for extras and standalone upgrades.

## Research and citation

Resources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614),
[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20614),
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.20614),
[BibTeX](https://arxiv.org/bibtex/2608.20614), and the
[NVIDIA Developer blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/).
Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff).

## Documentation

See [the documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) for
setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and
[performance dashboard](docs/reports.mdx#performance-dashboard). To let an agent run
SkillEvaluator, install [`skills/skillevaluator/`](skills/skillevaluator/).

## Installation and third-party software

Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation)
to choose the full installation or a smaller per-tier setup.

This project will download and install additional third-party open source
software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before
use.

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run:

```bash
make lint && make test && make build
```

See [project governance](GOVERNANCE.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Support

Support level: **Experimental**. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA
or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through
[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues); see
[SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md).

## Security

Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub
issue.

## Releases

Release changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/releases).

## License

Apache License 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), and
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.

[build-system]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
requires = ["setuptools >= 77", "wheel"]

[project]
name = "skillevaluator"
version = "0.8.0"
description = "Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills with quality gates, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation."
authors = [{ name = "NVIDIA Corporation" }]
readme = "README.md"
keywords = [
    "skills-evaluation",
    "skills",
    "skill-uplift",
    "ai-agents",
    "security",
    "vulnerability-scanner",
    "claude-code",
]
classifiers = [
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Quality Assurance",
]
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = [
    "LICENSE",
    "NOTICE",
    "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md",
]
# Base install is static-validation capable (Tier 1) and must NOT pull Harbor
# or LLM clients. Those live behind the extras below.
dependencies = [
    "click>=8.3.3,<9",
    "idna>=3.10,<4",
    "jinja2>=3.1",
    "markdown-it-py>=4.2,<5",
    "packaging>=24",
    "pydantic>=2.11.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # Dataset-authored signal patterns require a per-match timeout.
    "regex>=2024.11.6",
    "rich>=13.5.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Shared public LLM / embedding clients used by LLM-backed checks, Tier 2, and Tier 3.
llm = [
    "anthropic>=0.83.0",
    "boto3>=1.34.0",
    "litellm>=1.92.0,<1.94.0.dev0",
    "openai>=2.21.0",
]
# Tier 2 intra-skill deduplication and local-catalog inter-skill similarity.
tier2 = [
    "skillevaluator[llm]",
]
# Tier 3 live agent evaluation through Harbor's native environments.
tier3 = [
    "skillevaluator[llm]",
    "harbor[gke]==0.25.0",
    # CVE-2026-59950, CVE-2026-52870, and CVE-2026-52869 fixed floor.
    "mcp>=1.28.1,<2",
    # CVE-2026-48522 through CVE-2026-48526 fixed floor.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.13.0",
    # GHSA-hj66-6f7g-4r5v and GHSA-xpv3-w29h-x7cv fixed floor (via harbor[gke]).
    "oauthlib>=4.0.0",
    # PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED, which keeps Harbor from loading .env files, needs 1.2.0.
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.0",
]
# Static security scanners (floors raised to the established release baseline).
security = [
    "bandit>=1.9.4",
    "pip-audit>=2.10.0",
]
# Verify GitHub-signed execution receipts for the optional CI report publisher.
publisher = [
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.13.0",
]
# Optional local UI for comparing saved reports; never imported by base commands.
dashboard = [
    # server.allowedHosts, which limits the dashboard to loopback host names, needs 1.61.
    "streamlit>=1.61,<2",
]
# Full public install convenience bundle.
all = [
    "skillevaluator[tier2,tier3,security]",
]
dev = [
    "skillevaluator[publisher]",
    # PyPA build backs the `make build` target.
    "build>=1.2",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "pytest>=8.4.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.2.0",
    # pytest-xdist carried over for parallel test execution (-n auto).
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6.0",
    # Ruff 0.16 enables new rules that require a dedicated repository-wide cleanup.
    "ruff>=0.15.4,<0.16",
]

[project.urls]
Documentation = "https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator#readme"
Repository = "https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator"

[project.scripts]
# Single console script for the consolidated distribution.
skillevaluator = "skillevaluator.cli:cli"

[tool.uv]
managed = true

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["skillevaluator*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"skillevaluator.tier3" = ["grader_reference/*.json", "grader_reference/trajectories/*.json"]
"skillevaluator" = ["ci-release.json", "ci-release-all-tiers.json"]
"skillevaluator.config" = ["*.yaml", "profiles/*.yaml"]
"skillevaluator.reporting" = ["templates/*.j2", "assets/*.js", "assets/*.md"]
"skillevaluator.tier3.harbor" = [
    "templates/*.py",
    "templates/*.sh",
]
"skillevaluator.tier3.reference_skills" = [
    "*/SKILL.md",
    "*/evals/*.json",
    "*/evals/*.jsonl",
    "*/evals/*.yaml",
    "*/evals/*.yml",
    "*/evals/harbor/**/*",
    "*/evals/files/**/*",
    "*/references/**/*",
    "*/scripts/*.py",
    "*/scripts/*.sh",
    "*/files/**/*",
    "*/environment/docker-compose*.yml",
    "*/environment/docker-compose*.yaml",
    "*/mcp_servers.toml",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src", "tests"]
exclude = ["**/evals/results/**", ".venv", "build", "dist"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Union of the established rule selections and the broader static-analysis set.
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "B", "A", "COM", "C4", "DTZ", "T10", "EXE", "FA", "ISC", "ICN", "G", "INP", "PIE", "T20", "Q", "RSE", "RET", "SLF", "SLOT", "SIM", "TID", "TCH", "INT", "ARG", "PTH", "TD", "FIX"

name: substrate
description: Agent Substrate: the core system
readme_content:
# Agent Substrate **Zero-trust sandboxing for millions of agents on Kubernetes.** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/agent-substrate/substrate)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/pr-workflow.yaml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/pr-workflow.yaml?query=branch%3Amain) [![govulncheck](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yaml) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/agent-substrate/substrate?style=flat)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/stargazers) [Quickstart](#quickstart-development) · [Security](docs/security/security.md) · [Architecture](docs/concepts/architecture.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
## What is Agent Substrate? Agent Substrate is a security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. Purpose-built for the era of autonomous agents, Substrate delivers fast resume operations in less than 500ms, with more than 500 activations per second. Agents get isolated compute, identity, networking, and storage. Sensitive credentials are kept out of reach from untrusted code. It supports multiple sandbox technologies, including microVMs and gVisor, while enabling a consistent lifecycle and management of all sandboxes. At its core, Agent Substrate maps a larger set of “actors” (stateful workloads such as agents) onto a smaller pool of ready “workers”. Because agents spend most of their lives waiting on models, tools, or humans, Substrate snapshots idle actors out of memory and restores them when a request arrives. Substrate is a low-opinion runtime, not an agent SDK. The workloads it runs do not have to be AI agents, though autonomous, untrusted, mostly-idle agents are the target for its isolation and scheduling model. It runs on standard Kubernetes: Pods, autoscaling, NetworkPolicies. It adds agent-specific scheduling, snapshotting, identity, and network mediation. This allows agentic, inference, training, and reinforcement learning workloads to share one infrastructure plane. ## Security Model Substrate treats every actor as untrusted and mutually hostile, so tenants can share physical nodes without sharing a security boundary. Every control operates within the cold-start and resume budget. See the [Security Guide](docs/security/security.md) for the full list of security principles and threat model. * **Always sandboxed, VM-grade boundaries:** Every actor runs inside a dedicated [gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/) (`runsc`) or [Cloud Hypervisor](https://www.cloudhypervisor.org/) microVM sandbox with segregated compute, network, and storage. Plain Linux containers are not supported. * **Per-agent cryptographic identity:** Every active actor receives a short-lived [SPIFFE](https://spiffe.io/) X.509 certificate by default, and the egress gateway can mint per-actor JWTs on demand when an egress policy calls for one. Both carry the actor identity and atespace (the Substrate namespace grouping), and are designed to federate with external identity systems. * **Zero credentials in the sandbox:** Actors never hold actor identity JWTs/certs, API keys, or cloud tokens. The built-in egress gateway ([`atenet-egress`](docs/guides/egress-credential-injection.md)) injects credentials into approved outbound requests outside the sandbox, so a prompt-injected or compromised agent has nothing to exfiltrate. * **Default-deny networking:** Actors start with a private network stack, no inbound path except through the ingress router (`atenet-router`), no lateral actor-to-actor or control-plane access, and outbound traffic [restricted by the egress gateway](docs/guides/egress-traffic.md). * **Pluggable policy at the edge:** The egress gateway acts as an external Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) that is fully replaceable, allowing you to attach your own authorization, DLP, prompt-injection scanning, or cloud IAM policy engine without placing policy code inside the untrusted sandbox. ## Performance & Multiplexing [![Agent Substrate Demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/ZEzkCFJkzjY/hq1.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEzkCFJkzjY) *Watch the Agent Substrate cluster multiplex ~250 stateful actors across just 8 physical pods.* This demo highlights the core developer experience and "Agentic Infrastructure" capabilities of Substrate: 1. **Actor Teleport:** Suspend and resume actors onto any available worker in the pool, when needed. 2. **Full-State Persistence:** Working memory (RAM) and filesystem state are captured in snapshots and restored intact across hibernation cycles, without losing in-flight sessions or tool state. 3. **10x–30x Oversubscription:** Multiplex a large registry of stateful actors onto a small pool of warm worker pods, paying for compute only while an agent is actively thinking or executing a tool. To reproduce this demo in your own cluster, see the **[Counter Demo](demos/counter/README.md)**. For more walkthroughs, visit the **[agent-substrate YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCN9PPqlTtVxlcpbQ-NWpfZQ)**. ## Star History ## Framework Agnostic & Compatibility Agent Substrate is **framework and agent harness agnostic**. Because it runs standard OCI container images inside gVisor or microVM sandboxes and enforces security outside the workload, it hosts agents built on any stack without SDK changes: * **Agent Development Kit (ADK):** Preserves session state across invocations as actor state. * **LangChain:** Drop-in execution environment for LangChain agents and tool calls. * **Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity:** High-density, stateful coding environments that keep system and filesystem state across sessions while isolating untrusted code execution. * **Model Context Protocol (MCP):** Deploy sandboxed MCP servers as Substrate Actors with per-actor identity and egress controls. ## Ecosystem & Examples * **[Agent Executor](https://github.com/google/ax):** A distributed agent runtime that demonstrates building a secure, hyper-scalable agent harness on Agent Substrate (see the [announcement blog](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/agent-executor-googles-distributed-agent-runtime) and [integration guide](https://github.com/google/ax#2-deploy-the-control-plane)). * **[kagent](https://github.com/kagent-dev/kagent):** A CNCF Sandbox project and Kubernetes-native framework for building, deploying, and managing AI agents that uses Agent Substrate to run sandboxed, stateful agent workloads (see the [announcement blog](https://kagent.dev/blog/the-future-of-kagent)). ## Status and compatibility Agent Substrate has reached 1.0. We are committed to compatibility and stability of the public API, CLI, and configuration formats. We will continue to add new features, but we will not break existing APIs or configuration formats without a major version bump. See "Compatibility and schema evolution" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details. ### Supported Kubernetes Releases Currently we aim to support the [latest stable release](https://kubernetes.io/releases/) of Kubernetes, and the previous minor release. ## Community For announcements, technical discussions, and community support, please join the **[ate-dev](https://groups.google.com/g/ate-dev)** Google Group. We host a weekly community meeting every Thursday from 10:00am - 11:00am PST. - Video call link: https://meet.google.com/uhq-cxvn-dhy - Or dial: (US) +1 253-289-6971 PIN: 787 664 574 59# - More phone numbers: https://tel.meet/uhq-cxvn-dhy?pin=9044088223662 - [Meeting notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1obSIvfcafLNniLYTQCcT2eCgxHqa2AQ3Ga7YTsju49s) for the weekly sync meeting - [Recordings and transcripts](https://drive.google.com/corp/drive/u/0/folders/1rX1S6vPxPrR8dA1lEBuBEXkGKjHtG-mL) of all community meetings We also have channels in the CNCF slack; [request an invite here](https://slack.cncf.io/) if you don't have access. - [#substrate-users](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C0B6RCAJULW) to discuss using substrate. - [#substrate-dev](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C0B6M3E2J3D) to discuss developing substrate. ## Developing Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines on contributing to the project. We welcome contributions of all kinds, but the project is VERY young. Our immediate focus is on building out the core system and demos, so we may not be able to review or merge contributions that don't align with those goals in the near term. ## Quickstart (Development) To quickly set up the complete environment: 1. Make sure you have [Go](https://go.dev/doc/install), [`kubectl`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/), and [`docker`](https://www.docker.com/) installed and configured on your dev machine. We will automatically manage other dependencies via Go, including [`kind`](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/). A Linux host that will run more than about a thousand sandboxes also needs a larger kernel neighbor table (`net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh1/2/3` = 4096/16384/32768); `hack/create-kind-cluster.sh` warns when the host is at the default of 1024. 2. Run the following steps: ```shell # create cluster and local registry hack/create-kind-cluster.sh # make ate-setup target the kind cluster; set this in every shell that runs # ate-setup, including for the demo walkthroughs export ATE_INSTALL_KIND=true # install Substrate go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy ate-system --credential-provider='{"name":"k8s.io"}' \ --ingress-allowed-spiffe-ids=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/ate-system/sa/atenet-client # install counter demo go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy demo counter # install kubectl-ate go install ./cmd/kubectl-ate # create a counter actor in the demo's atespace (--template names the # actor template, resolved in the actor's atespace) kubectl ate create actor my-counter-1 -a ate-demo-counter --template counter # serve a local proxy on port 8000 that sends requests to the actor through the # network router kubectl ate proxy actor my-counter-1 -a ate-demo-counter ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > `{"name":"k8s.io"}` deploys the bundled credential provider with an empty, > default-deny namespace policy. Before an actor can have a credential > injected, grant its atespace the namespaces whose Secrets it may read; see > [Enable it](docs/guides/egress-credential-injection.md#enable-it). 3. # The Go Programming Language

Go is an open source programming language that makes it easy to build simple,
reliable, and efficient software.

![Gopher image](https://golang.org/doc/gopher/fiveyears.jpg)
*Gopher image by [Renee French][rf], licensed under [Creative Commons 4.0 Attribution license][cc4-by].*

Our canonical Git repository is located at https://go.googlesource.com/go.
There is a mirror of the repository at https://github.com/golang/go.

Unless otherwise noted, the Go source files are distributed under the
BSD-style license found in the LICENSE file.

### Download and Install

#### Binary Distributions

Official binary distributions are available at https://go.dev/dl/.

After downloading a binary release, visit https://go.dev/doc/install
for installation instructions.

#### Install From Source

If a binary distribution is not available for your combination of
operating system and architecture, visit
https://go.dev/doc/install/source
for source installation instructions.

### Contributing

Go is the work of thousands of contributors. We appreciate your help!

To contribute, please read the contribution guidelines at https://go.dev/doc/contribute.

Note that the Go project uses the issue tracker for bug reports and
proposals only. See https://go.dev/wiki/Questions for a list of
places to ask questions about the Go language.

readme_content:
Appwrite

The open-source cloud for agents and developers. Appwrite is an MCP and agent-first platform for building and scaling apps. Give your agents Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Messaging, Realtime, and Hosting, all in one place.

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://appwrite.io/discord) [![X](https://img.shields.io/badge/follow-000000?style=flat-square&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/appwrite) [![Appwrite Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloud-F02E65?style=flat-square&logo=icloud&logoColor=white)](https://cloud.appwrite.io) English | [简体中文](README-CN.md) Appwrite is an MCP and agent-first, open-source platform for building and scaling apps. MCP is included, so coding agents can operate on a live Appwrite project. Appwrite is available as a managed cloud platform and can also be self-hosted on infrastructure you control. It is designed for the AI agents in your workflow as well as for developers. Connect Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and other agents through the hosted MCP server, or integrate an SDK into your app. Modular products stay unified from the first prototype to production scale. Find out more at [https://appwrite.io](https://appwrite.io). Table of Contents: - [Products](#products) - [Installation \& Setup](#installation--setup) - [Self-Hosting](#self-hosting) - [Unix](#unix) - [Windows](#windows) - [CMD](#cmd) - [PowerShell](#powershell) - [Docker API version mismatch](#docker-api-version-mismatch) - [Upgrade from an Older Version](#upgrade-from-an-older-version) - [One-Click Setups](#one-click-setups) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [Agents](#agents) - [SDKs](#sdks) - [Client](#client) - [Server](#server) - [Architecture](#architecture) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Security](#security) - [Follow Us](#follow-us) - [License](#license) ## Products - **[Appwrite Auth](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/auth)** - Authenticate users securely with email, SMS, OAuth, anonymous sessions, and magic URLs. - **[Appwrite Databases](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/databases)** - Model, query, and scale with Appwrite databases or managed PostgreSQL and MySQL, so you can match your use case and team needs. - **[Appwrite Storage](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/storage)** - Store files with compression, encryption, image transformations, and access control. - **[Appwrite Functions](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/functions)** - Deploy serverless functions with secure isolated runtimes and event-driven execution. - **[Appwrite Sites](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/sites)** - Deploy static, SSR, and CSR frontends from Git with instant previews and Appwrite behind them. - **[Appwrite Messaging](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/messaging)** - Send email, SMS, and push notifications through a unified messaging service. - **[Appwrite Firewall](https://appwrite.io/docs/products/network)** - Protect apps with traffic rules, abuse controls, and edge security for every project. - **[Appwrite Realtime](https://appwrite.io/docs/apis/realtime)** - Subscribe and react to events across your project as they happen. - **[Appwrite MCP](https://appwrite.io/docs/tooling/ai/mcp-servers/api)** - Connect agents to your Appwrite project, APIs, and docs. MCP is included on Cloud, with no local install required. ## Installation & Setup The easiest way to get started with Appwrite is by [signing up for Appwrite Cloud](https://cloud.appwrite.io/). Cloud includes a [Free plan](https://appwrite.io/pricing) so you can start building immediately, with paid plans when you need to scale. ## Self-Hosting Appwrite was designed from the ground up with self-hosting in mind. You can install and run Appwrite on any operating system that can run a [Docker CLI](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop). Running your server is as easy as running one command from your terminal. Before running the installation command, make sure you have [Docker](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop) installed on your machine. The setup wizard listens on port **20080** and is published on localhost only. It also prints a one-time installer secret to STDOUT — open the printed URL (or send `x-appwrite-installer-secret`) to complete setup. For a remote host, SSH-tunnel to `127.0.0.1:20080` rather than publishing the port on all interfaces. ### Unix ```bash docker run -it --rm \ --publish 127.0.0.1:20080:20080 \ --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ --volume "$(pwd)"/appwrite:/usr/src/code/appwrite:rw \ --entrypoint="install" \ appwrite/appwrite:2.7.2 ``` ### Windows #### CMD ```cmd docker run -it --rm ^ --publish 127.0.0.1:20080:20080 ^ --volume //var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ^ --volume "%cd%"/appwrite:/usr/src/code/appwrite:rw ^ --entrypoint="install" ^ appwrite/appwrite:2.7.2 ``` #### PowerShell ```powershell docker run -it --rm ` --publish 127.0.0.1:20080:20080 ` --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ` --volume ${pwd}/appwrite:/usr/src/code/appwrite:rw ` --entrypoint="install" ` appwrite/appwrite:2.7.2 ``` Once the installer is running, open the URL printed in the terminal (it includes a one-time secret) to complete the setup wizard. After installation, go to http://localhost to access the Appwrite console from your browser. Please note that on non-Linux native hosts, the server might take a few minutes to start after completing the installation. ### Docker API version mismatch If install or upgrade fails with an error like `client version 1.52 is too new. Maximum supported API version is 1.42`, the Docker CLI inside the Appwrite image is newer than your host Docker Engine. Pass `DOCKER_API_VERSION` set to the maximum API version from the error (or upgrade Docker on the host): ```bash docker run -it --rm \ --env DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.42 \ --publish 127.0.0.1:20080:20080 \ --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ --volume "$(pwd)"/appwrite:/usr/src/code/appwrite:rw \ --entrypoint="install" \ appwrite/appwrite:2.7.2 ``` Use the same `--env DOCKER_API_VERSION=...` flag with `--entrypoint="upgrade"` when upgrading. For advanced production and custom installation, check out our Docker [environment variables](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/configuration/environment-variables) docs. You can also use our public [docker-compose.yml](https://appwrite.io/install/compose) and [.env](https://appwrite.io/install/env) files to manually set up an environment. ### Upgrade from an Older Version If you are upgrading your Appwrite server from an older version, you should use the Appwrite migration tool once your setup is completed. For more information regarding this, check out the [migration instructions](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/production/updates). ## One-Click Setups In addition to running Appwrite locally, you can launch Appwrite using a pre-configured marketplace app for instant setup. Choose from one of the providers below:

DigitalOcean
Gitpod
Akamai Compute
AWS Marketplace
For custom deployments on a cloud provider or PaaS, see the guides for [AWS](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/platforms/aws), [DigitalOcean](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/platforms/digitalocean), [Google Cloud](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/platforms/google-cloud), [Azure](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/platforms/azure), [Coolify](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/platforms/coolify), and [Dokploy](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/platforms/dokploy). ## Getting Started Getting started with Appwrite is as easy as creating a new project, connecting an agent, or integrating an SDK into your code. You can start from a prompt, a quick start tutorial, or the hosted MCP server. ### Agents Designed for the AI agents in your workflow. Query a database, chart traffic, or ship a change: your agent does it on a live Appwrite project. The hosted MCP server uses OAuth, so you do not need to create or manage API keys. For a self-hosted instance, use the [local MCP server](https://appwrite.io/docs/advanced/self-hosting/mcp) instead. Add the remote server to Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, and other MCP clients: ```json { "mcpServers": { "appwrite": { "url": "https://mcp.appwrite.io/" } } } ``` You can also [add the MCP server to Cursor](https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=appwrite&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5hcHB3cml0ZS5pby8ifQ==) in one click. Install language-specific [agent skills](https://appwrite.io/docs/tooling/ai/skills) so models generate correct SDK calls: ```bash npx skills add appwrite/agent-skills ``` Browse [quick start prompts](https://appwrite.io/docs/tooling/ai/quickstart-prompts), generate an [AGENTS.md](https://appwrite.io/docs/tooling/ai/agents-md) file for your repo, or see the [AI tooling docs](https://appwrite.io/docs/tooling/ai) for IDE and vibe coding setup. Getting started with your platform of choice is also covered in the tutorials below. | Platform | Technology | | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Web app** | [Quick start for Web](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/web) | | | [Quick start for Next.js](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/nextjs) | | | [Quick start for React](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/react) | | | [Quick start for Vue.js](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/vue) | | | [Quick start for Nuxt](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/nuxt) | | | [Quick start for SvelteKit](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/sveltekit) | | | [Quick start for Astro](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/astro) | | | [Quick start for TanStack Start](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/tanstack-start) | | | [Quick start for Refine](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/refine) | | | [Quick start for Angular](https://appwrite.io/docs/quick-starts/angular) | | **Mobile and Native** | [Quick s

readme_content: # Kubernetes (K8s) [![CII Best Practices](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/569/badge)](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/569) ![GitHub release (latest SemVer)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kubernetes/kubernetes?sort=semver) ---- Kubernetes, also known as K8s, is an open source system for managing [containerized applications] across multiple hosts. It provides basic mechanisms for the deployment, maintenance, and scaling of applications. Kubernetes builds upon a decade and a half of experience at Google running production workloads at scale using a system called [Borg], combined with best-of-breed ideas and practices from the community. Kubernetes is hosted by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation ([CNCF]). If your company wants to help shape the evolution of technologies that are container-packaged, dynamically scheduled, and microservices-oriented, consider joining the CNCF. For details about who's involved and how Kubernetes plays a role, read the CNCF [announcement]. ---- ## To start using K8s See our documentation on [kubernetes.io]. Take a free course on [Scalable Microservices with Kubernetes]. To use Kubernetes code as a library in other applications, see the [list of published components](https://git.k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/README.md). Use of the `k8s.io/kubernetes` module or `k8s.io/kubernetes/...` packages as libraries is not supported. ## To start developing K8s The [community repository] hosts all information about building Kubernetes from source, how to contribute code and documentation, who to contact about what, etc. If you want to build Kubernetes right away there are two options: ##### You have a working [Go environment]. ``` git clone https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes cd kubernetes make ``` ##### You have a working [Docker environment]. ``` git clone https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes cd kubernetes make quick-release ``` For the full story, head over to the [developer's documentation]. ## Support If you need support, start with the [troubleshooting guide], and work your way through the process that we've outlined. That said, if you have questions, reach out to us [one way or another][communication]. This is Python version 3.16.0 alpha 2+dev
=========================================

.. image:: https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?branch=main&event=push
